【29】DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS

【30】 Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PCP): Given the patient’s immunocompromised status, his low-grade fever, and his presentation with increasing dyspnea over 1 week, this is the favored diagnosis. The progression of the lung abnormalities from perihilar reticulation to more extensive bilateral opacification is common in untreated pneumocystis pneumonia. Furthermore, pneumothorax is a common complication of PCP.

【31】 Noncardiogenic edema: Permeability edema due to a variety of causes including sepsis and drug toxicity may have a virtually identical radiographic appearance, and may result in reticular opacities that progress to diffuse parenchymal opacification. Furthermore, if the permeability edema develops into adult respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), the lung becomes noncom-pliant and pneumothorax may develop. However, most causes of permeability edema result in a very acute presentation rather than dyspnea that progresses over 1 week, as was seen in this patient. Acute interstitial pneumonia (AIP), which is a rare entity and which essentially represents idiopathic ARDS, can present over a longer period of time than other forms of ARDS and is a consideration in this patient. However, the clinical history would strongly favor PCP; there is no association between brain tumors, corticosteroid use, and AIP.

【32】 Collagen vascular diseases: Wegener’s granulomatosis and systemic lupus erythematosus may cause diffuse alveolar hemorrhage (DAH), which in turn may result in extensive multifocal ground glass, as seen in this patient. However, the initial radiograph demonstrating reticular opacities would be atypical for hemorrhage. Furthermore, patients with DAH generally present with hemoptysis rather than fever and shortness of breath.

【33】DIAGNOSIS

【34】Pneumocystis jioveci pneumonia (PCP)

【35】KEY FACTS

【36】Clinical

【37】 The organism originally thought to be responsible for pneumocystis pneumonia in humans was Pneumocystis carinii . However, phenotypic differences were discovered between the organism that infects humans and the organism that infects other mammals, and in 2001 the name Pneumocystis jirovecii was chosen to designate the species that infects humans. The acronym “PCP” has remained in use, formed from Pneumo Cystis Pneumonia.

【38】 Pneumocystis , initially considered a trypanosome, was then reclassified as a protozoan; it is now phylogeneti-cally considered to be a fungus.

【39】 In the United States, clinically identifiable disease manifests in severely immunocompromised patients. Patients considered to be at high risk for Pneumocystis infection include patients who are positive for the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) with a CD4 count of <200 cells/uL; non-HIV immunocompromised patients with hematologic malignancies or solid tumors (particularly patients with brain tumors treated with high-dose corticosteroids); patients who have undergone solid organ or bone marrow transplantation; patients on high-dose corticosteroid therapy; and patients with primary immunodeficiencies.

【40】 Symptoms are generally nonspecific, including fever, dyspnea, and nonproductive cough. Symptoms in HIV-infected individuals often present with a more subacute course, with symptoms progressing over 3 to 4 weeks rather than the progression of symptoms over approximately 1 week in other immunosuppressed individuals.

【41】 The diagnosis is made by observing organisms on induced sputum, bronchoalveolar lavage, or lung biopsy specimens.

【42】 Prophylaxis with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxasole (TMP-SMX) therapy has been effective in decreasing the number of patients presenting with Pneumocystis pneumonia. Dapsone or aerosolized pentamadine are considered less effective as prophylaxis, and are generally used when side effects from TMP-SMX cannot be tolerated.

【43】 Treatment is generally with TMP-SMX or pentamidine. Dapsone, or clindamycin-primaquine have also been used. The use of steroids in treatment is controversial.

【44】 Response to therapy is generally excellent. Clinical improvement is typically seen within several days. Nevertheless, some patients will proceed to respiratory failure, requiring stringent therapeutic supportive measures.

【45】Radiologic

【46】 PCP typically manifests with diffuse, bilateral, fine to medium reticulonodular opacities. These reticular opacities are often perihilar in distribution. If untreated, the reticular opacities may progress to diffuse ground glass, which is often granular in appearance.

【47】 At the time of initial presentation with symptoms, the radiograph may be normal.

【48】 Unusual appearances include focal homogeneous opacities and larger (1 to 2 cm) nodules, with or without cavitation. Pleural effusions and lymphadenopathy are extremely rare.

【49】 Pneumatoceles are seen in approximately 10% of patients with PCP, and may take months to resolve. Fluid levels within pneumatoceles are extremely rare and should suggest superinfection.

【50】 Spontaneous pneumothorax occurs in 5% to 6% of patients with PCP, and the presence of pneumatoceles increases the risk of pneumothorax formation.

【51】 On CT, particularly HRCT, multifocal ground glass is the most common finding. The ground glass may be geographic in distribution. Other CT findings may include consolidation, cysts, and a “crazy paving” pattern of interlobular septal thickening superimposed on regions of ground glass opacity.

【52】 HRCT may be helpful in demonstrating ground glass abnormalities in patients with a normal radiograph. Additionally, CT may be used by bronchoscopists as a “roadmap” to determine which segments to target for bronchoalveolar lavage.

【53】 With appropriate therapy, the abnormalities (other than the pneumatoceles) may resolve in as quickly as 10 days. Occasionally, residual fibrosis is observed.

【54】 Due to the fact that patients with PCP are immunocom-promised, they may be infected with more than one organism. Imaging may be helpful in suggesting the presence of multiple infectious agents. For example, if PCP is suspected in a patient with multifocal ground glass, the presence of a pleural effusion should initiate a search for an additional organism, since pleural effusions are extremely rare in the setting of PCP. Diagnosis usually requires bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage.

【57】Chong S, Lee KS, Yi CA, et al. Pulmonary fungal infection: imaging findings in immunocompromised and immunocompetent patients. Eur J Radiol 2006;59:371–383.

CHRISTENSEN

【60】HISTORY

【61】A 44-year-old female smoker with slowly progressive dyspnea and cough.

【62】通用删除16(英):<u> FIGURE 1-24A Posteroanterior chest radiograph. Diffuse bilateral heterogenous mixed alveolar and interstitial reticular opacities with relative apical sparing. The heart is of normal size. There are no pleural effusions.</u>

【63】通用删除16(英):<u> FIGURE 1-24B Representative axial high-resolution chest CT image (lung window). Bilateral geographic ground glass opacities with smooth interlobular septal thickening extending to the pleural surface are present. No appreciable pulmonary nodules or consolidation.</u>

【64】DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS

【65】 Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis: Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (PAP) manifests radiographically as central and symmetric alveolar opacities, often sparing the lung apices and costophrenic sulci. CT features thickening of the interlobular septa with a background of ground glass opacities, a pattern referred to as “crazy paving.” Pulmonary fibrosis occurs in advanced disease. Given the clinical history and radiologic features, this is the most likely diagnosis.

【66】 Pulmonary edema: Pulmonary edema may be caused by increased pulmonary venous pressure (hydrostatic) or capillary permeability (nonhydrostatic). Common hydrostatic etiologies include left-sided heart failure, volume overload, or renal failure. Diffuse alveolar opacities represent the most advanced form of hydrostatic pulmonary edema. A common manifestation of nonhydrostatic edema is ARDS, which represents the most severe form of diffuse lung injury (DLI), characterized by diffuse alveolar damage, resulting in increased capillary permeability. The onset of dyspnea related to edema may be sudden, unlike the presented case, and in the setting of hydrostatic edema, the clinical symptoms may fluctuate.

【67】 Hypersensitivity pneumonitis (HP): CL nodules with ground glass opacities with basilar sparing are characteristic of this disorder. The lung apices are routinely involved. The presented case does not exhibit pulmonary nodules, and demonstrates relative sparing of the apices, making this a less likely option.

【68】 Pulmonary hemorrhage: DAH results in ground glass opacities, which may progress to areas of confluent consolidation. Etiologies are diverse and include Wegener’s granulomatosis, anti-glomerular basement membrane (anti-GBM) syndrome, vasculitides, and connective tissue disorders, such as systemic lupus erythematosis (SLE). The onset is typically more sudden than in the presented case, making this diagnosis less likely.

【69】 Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PCP): The alveolar opacities associated with PCP are classically perihi-lar in distribution, but can be diffuse with progressive disease and during the course of steroid treatment. Pneumocystis jirovecii is one of several infections that may present as diffuse alveolar opacities, particularly in immunocompromised patients; other pathogens include cytomegalovirus (CMV) and herpes simplex virus (HSV).

【70】 Invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma (formerly bronchioloalveolar cell carcinoma, or BAC): This malignancy most often presents as a focal, subpleural consolidation with areas of ground glass opacities. When the lung is diffusely involved, ground glass opacities are a predominant feature, but rarely occur without associated multifocal consolidation. The lack of consolidation despite diffuse lung involvement in the presented case makes this a less likely diagnosis.

【71】DIAGNOSIS

【72】Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis

【73】KEY FACTS

【74】Clinical

【75】 Patients with PAP accumulate abnormal amounts of surfactant within the alveoli, which subsequently interferes with capillary oxygen diffusion. Patients therefore often present with profound hypoxia, which may be chronic and slowly progressive.

【76】 Primary causes include idiopathic (accounting for 90% of all cases) and hereditary forms of the disease. Secondary PAP is associated with lymphoproliferative disorders and occupational exposure to silica, aluminum, and titanium dusts. There is a high association with smoking (>70%).

【77】 Patients with PAP are at risk for superimposed infection with atypical pathogens, particularly Nocardia , but also including Aspergillus, Cryptococcus neoformans, Candida, pneumocystis jirovecii , and both tuberculous and nontuberculous mycobacteria.

【78】 The primary treatment for PAP focuses on removing excess surfactant from the alveoli via whole lung lavage. Posttreatment radiographs may demonstrate increased alveolar opacities due to retained fluid and should not be confused with disease progression.

【79】 Approximately a third of patients have spontaneous remission, a third have persistent disease requiring whole lung lavage, and a third progress to pulmonary fibrosis despite therapy.

【80】Radiologic

【81】 Findings on chest radiography are highly variable and correlate to disease burden. The classic presentation is bilateral central and symmetric opacities with sparing of the apices and costophrenic angles. However, radiographs may be normal, demonstrate multifocal opacities, or exhibit diffuse alveolar opacities, as in the case presented.

【82】 Pleural effusions and cardiomegaly are typically absent.

【83】 The characteristic CT features of PAP are diffuse ground glass opacities with smooth interlobular sep-tal thickening—an appearance referred to as “crazy-paving.” The crazy-paving pattern is seen in a broad variety of diffuse lung diseases, but has the highest prevalence in PAP.

【84】 PAP often spares the lung apices and costophrenic sulci. Subpleural sparing is seen in up to 50%.

【85】 Imaging findings in conjunction with appropriate clinical presentation are suggestive; however, bronchoalve-olar lavage or biopsy is required for definitive diagnosis.

【101】**N their fully developed form， allergic contact der-matitis and irritant contact dermatitis are both intra-epidermal vesicular dermatitides that appear after exposure to different kinds of contactants， namely， allergens in the former and irritant substances in the latter.**

【102】Histopathologically， allergic and irritant contact dermatitides have in common intra- and intercellular edema， edema of the papillary dermis， and superficial perivascular mixed inflammatory-cell infiltrates. Both also may be associated with subepidermal vesiculation. In allergic contact dermatitis， that occurrence is secondary to either bursting of intra-epidermal spongiotic vesicles or extensive edema of the papillary dermis. In irritant contact der-matitis， that phenomenon comes about as a consequence of rupture of intra-epidermal ballooning vesicles or of sevveereepidermalnecrosis with subsequent dermo-epidermal separation.

【103】Allergic contact dermatitis results from exposure of previously sensi-tized persons to contact allergens. It is a delayed type of hypersensitivity reaction， in contrast to irritant contact dermatitis， which is not a hypersen-sitivity reaction at all. Irritant contact dermatitis results from direct injury to the skin by a variety of agents such as strong acids and alkalis， and by less irritating substances such as croton oil and sodium lauryl sulfate.

【104】Clinically， allergic contact dermatitis appears as edematous pink pap-ules that soon become papulovesicles. That these are actually vesicles often can be appreciated better by gentle palpation than by observation. With progression， the vesicles become discernible clearly and， in severe cases， huge bullae may form. Biopsy specimens taken serially reveal the early stage of allergic contact dermatitis to consist of spongiosis that becomes decidedly focal (spongiotic dermatitis)， a fully developed stage that shows epidermal hyperplasia in addition to spongiotic vesicles (spongiotic psoriasiform der-matitis)， and a late stage in which there is psoriasiform hyperplasia (psori-asiform dermatitis) devoid of spongiosis. In long-enduringlesions of allergic contact dermatitis， there usually are histopathologic evidences of persistent rubbing (i.e.， lichen simplex chronicus) in the form of a papillary dermis thickened by coarse bundles of collagen arranged in vertical streaks and of compact orthokeratosis.

The histopathologic differential diagnosis of allergic contact dermatitis at all stages of the process involves consideration ofearly nummular derma-titis， dyshidrotic dermatitis， “id”reactions， and vesicular dermatophytic in-fections， all of which may show the same histopathologic features in sec-tions stained by hematoxylin and eosin. The presence of hyphae within the cornified layer establishes the diagnosis of dermatophytosis. The other four|删除1换行|conditions cannot be differentiated histopathologically from one another. Some patients may present themselves with widespread papulovesicular， vesicular， and even bullous eruptions that on the hands and feet may be interpreted as dyshidrotic dermatitis and “id”reactions， on other arcas of the integument as allergic contact dermatitis， and on other sites as nummu-lar dermatitis. Given this circumstance clinically and the identity of these four conditions histopathologically， these four spongiotic dermatitides seem to be related to one another.

【106】Photo-allergic contact dermatitis， such as to salicylanilides， and photo-allergic dermatitis， such as to systemically administered chlorpromazine， are similar histopathologically to allergic contact dermatitis， except that in the photodermatitides the infiltrate of inflammatory cells tends to be both deep as well as superficial， and the epidermis tends to harbor a few necrotic keratinocytes. Clinically， photo-allergic contact dermatitis and photo-aller-gic dermatitis usually are confined to regions of the skin that ordinarily are exposed to sunlight.

【107】Irritant contact dermatitis may range clinically from slight erythema and scaling to severe blisters and ulcerations. Like allergic contact dermati-tis， irritant contact dermatitis has a photo-related counterpart， namely， _一_ phototoxic contact dermatitis caused by substances that become irritants only afler photo-activation. Phototoxic dermatitis may result from systemi-cally administered chemicals such as psoralens， and phototoxic contact der-matitis may result from chemicals such as psoralens applied topically. The phototoxic lesions are similar to irritant contact dermatitis clinically and histopathologically， and they， too， occur only on areas exposed to ultraviolet light.

【9】**Non-Hodgkin's Lymphoma**

【10】Non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma (NHL) is a group of lymphomas affecting lymphoid tissue and occurring in persons of all ages. It is more common in adults in their middle and older years(40 to 60 years of age).

【11】**Risk Factors**

【12】Males are affected more often than females and individuals with congenital or acquired immunodeficiencies (e.g.， those undergoing organ transplantation and anyone with autoim-mune diseases are all at increased risk for development of NHL)1 In addition， some people who have been exposed to large levels of radiation (e.g.， nuclear reactor accidents) or extensive radiation and chemotherapy for a different cancer site may be at increased risk for lymphoma.

【13】Individuals infected with the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) are at increased risk for developing NHL and to a lesser extent， Hodgkin’s disease as well. AIDS-related lym-phoma (ARL) is now the second most common cancer asso-ciated with HIV after Kaposi’s sarcoma. The relative risk of developing lymphoma within 3 years of an AIDS diagnosis is increased by 165-fold compared with people without AIDS.1

【14】Several possible etiologic mechanisms are hypothesized for NHL. Immunosuppression， possibly in combination with viruses or exposure to certain infectious agents， could be the primary cause. Chemicals， UV light， blood transfusion， acquired and congenital immune deficiency， and autoim-mune disorders increase the risk for NHL.172

【15】Other studies link the disease to widespread environmen-tal contaminants such as benzene found in cigarette smoke， gasoline， automobile emissions， and industrial pollution.

【16】NHL presents a clinical picture broadly similar to that of Hodgkin’s disease， except that the disease is usually initially more widespread and less predictable. The disease starts in the lymph nodes， although early involvement of the oropha-ryngeal lymphoid tissue or the bone marrow is common， as is abdominal mass or GI involvement with complaints of vague back or abdominal discomfort.173

【17】The most common manifestation is painless enlargement of one or more peripheral lymph nodes. Systemic symptoms are not as commonly associated with NHL as with Hodgkin’s disease. Clients with NHLs often have remarkably few symp-toms， even though many node areas or extranodal sites are involved.

【18】Most NHLs fall into two broad categories related to their clinical activity： indolent and aggressive. Indolent disease may be minimally active and treatable for many years. How-ever， the disease is frequently disseminated at the time of diagnosis. Surgery is usually used only for staging or debulk-ing purposes. Combination chemotherapy， biotherapy (tar-geted monoclonal antibodies)， and radiation therapies are now used as treatment for NHL. Radioactive isotope combi-nations with monoclonal antibodies are also in use for some types of NHL.13

【21】**Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome-Non-Hodgkin's Lymphoma**

【22】Only recently has AIDS-NHL emerged as a major sequela of HIV infection. It now occurs frequently in clients who sur-vive other consequences of AIDS.

【23】The etiologic basis of AIDS-NHL is still under investiga-tion； profound cellular immunodeficiency plays a central role in lymphoma genesis. The molecular pathogenesis is a complex process involving both host factors and genetic alterations.174

【24】Nearly 95% of all HIV-associated malignancies are either NHL or Kaposi's sarcoma. People with CNS lymphoma usu-ally have advanced AIDS， are severely debilitated， and are usually thought to be at terminal stages of the disease.

【25】EBV often accompanies NHL. It is generally accepted that EBV acts in the pathogenesis of lymphoma owing to the alteration in balance between host and latent EBV infec-tion in immunodeficiency states， with increased activity of the virus.

【26】Infection with HIV and related immunodeficiencies resulting from HIV are the primary risk factors for this disease. NHL is more likely to develop among clients who have Kaposi’s sarcoma， a history of herpes simplex infection， and a lower neutrophil count.

【27】**Clinical Signs and Symptoms**

【28】The most common presentations of HIV-related NHL are systemic B symptoms (which may suggest an infectious pro-cess)， a rapidly enlarging mass lesion， or both. At the time of diagnosis， approximately 75% of clients will have advanced disease. Extranodal disease frequently involves any part of the body， with the most common locations being the CNS， bone marrow， GI tract， and liver.

【29】Diagnosis of NHL in areas of the body other than the CNS is complicated by a history of fevers， night sweats， and weight loss and loss of appetite， which are also common symptoms related to HIV infection and AIDS.

【30】Although musculoskeletal lesions are not reported as com-monly as pulmonary or CNS abnormalities in HIV-positive individuals， a wide variety of osseous and soft tissue changes are seen in this group. Diffuse adenopathy， lower extremity pain and swelling， subcutaneous nodules， and lytic lesions of the extremities are common.175

【33】**PHYSICIAN REFERRAL**

【34】Early detection of cancer can save a person’s life. Any suspi-cious sign or symptom discussed in this chapter should be investigated immediately by a physician. This is true espe-cially in the presence of a positive family history of cancer， a previous personal history of cancer， and environmental risk factors， and/or in the absence of medical or dental (oral) eval-uation during the previous year.

【35】The therapist is not responsible for diagnosing cancer. The primary goal in screening for cancer is to make sure the client’s problem is within the scope of a physical therapist’s practice. In this regard， documentation of key findings and communication with the physician are both very important.

【36】When trying to sort out neurologic findings， remember to look for changes in DTRs， a myotomal weakness pattern， and changes in bowel/bladder function. These findings will not give you a definitive diagnosis but will provide you with valuable information to offer the physician if further medical testing is advised.

Pain while weight-bearing that is unrelieved by rest or change in position and does not respond to treatment，|删除1换行|unremitting pain at night， and a history of cancer are all red flags indicating that medical evaluation is needed.

【38】Any recently discovered lumps or nodules must be exam-ined by a physician. Any suspicious finding by report， dur-ing observation， or by palpation should be checked by a physician.

【39】If any signs of skin lesions are described by the client or if they are observed by the therapist and the client has not been examined by a physician， a medical referral is recommended.

【40】If the client is planning a follow-up visit with the phy-sician within the next 2 to 4 weeks， that client is advised to indicate the mole or skin changes at that time. If no appointment is pending， the client is encouraged to make a specific visit either to the family/personal physician or to a dermatologist.

【25】**Spike vs. nonspike potentials on EEG**

【26】**· Spikes and sharp waves are fast transients. By definition， spikes are usually surface-negative and have a duration of 20-70 ms while sharp waves are also surface-negative but with a longer duration of 70-200 ms. A sharp wave should not be considered abnormal unless it stands out from the background and is reproducible.**

【27】**· One of the major pitfalls in EEG interpretation is misinterpreting sharply contoured rhythms as sharp waves and spikes. Examples include theta activity that can be pointed and looks like a run of spike-and-wave complexes.**

【34】**Epileptiform activity**

【35】**·Epileptiform activity is generated when depolarization of the cortex results in synchronous activation of many neurons.**

【36】**· The abnormalities in epileptiform activity are the repetitive nature of the discharge and the degree of the synchrony. In fact， synchronous activation of many neurons is required for generation of both normal and abnormal rhythms.**

【37】**1 Spike and sharp waves**

【38】◆ Epileptiform activities mainly consist of spikes and sharp waves. While epilep-tiform slow activity and suppression does occur， this is much less common.

【39】·When the depolarization spreads synchronously to many neurons through as-sociative connections， the summed field potentials are detected on the surface as a spike.

【40】·Spike waves have a duration of less than 70 ms.

【41】◆Sharp waves have a duration of 70-200 ms.

【42】**2 Paroxysmal depolarization shift (PDS)**

【43】◆ PDS comprises extracellular field potentials that are waves of depolarization followed by repolarization， reflecting the foundation of the bursting of spike discharges.

【53】**Hypsarrthythmia**

【54】**· Hypsarrthythmia is the interictal EEG pattern consisting of random high-voltage slow waves mixed with high-voltage multifocal spikes and sharp waves arising from all cortical regions.**

【55】**·Other variants have been described， including modified hypsarrhythmia and atypical hyparrhythmia.**

【84】**Brainstem auditory-evoked potentials (BAEPs)**

【85】**·Brainstem auditory-evoked potentials test acoustic conduction through the ear， the eighth cranial nerve， into the lower pons， and continuing rostrally in the lateral lemniscus up the brainstem.**

【86】**· In clinical practice， this is often used to screen hearing in infants. It is also performed in adults for evaluation of possible acoustic neuroma but it is less helpful when evaluating for multiple sclerosis， compared to visual evoked potentials (VEPs). It can also evaluate peripheral and central auditory pathway in sedated and anesthetized patients.**

【87】**拿The waves routinely analyzed in BAEPs testing are I through V. The several succeeding peaks VI-VIII are quite variable and are not used for interpretation.**

【88】**·Wave I： the eighth cranial nerve near the brainstem**

【89】**_◆_ Wave II： near or at the cochlear nucleus at the junction of pons and medulla**

【90】**_◆_ Wave III： lower pons in the region of superior olive and trapezoid body**

【91】**◆Wave Ⅳ， V： upper pons/lower midbrain in the lateral lemniscus or inferior colliculus**

【95】**·The somatosensory-evoked potential (SSEP) is the response to electrical stimulation of mixed or cutaneous peripheral nerves.**

【96】**· SSEPs are usually obtained in the upper extremity with stimulation of the median and ulnar nerves at the wrist， recording at Erb’s point in the supraclavicular fossa (N9， afferent volley in plexus)， the neck 通用删除11(英):<u>(P14， caudal medial lemniscus)</u>， and the scalp (N20， thalamocortical radiations).**

【97】**· In the lower extremity， the responses are obtained with stimulation of the tibial or peroneal nerves at the ankle， with recording over the lumbar spine(N22， dorsal roots and entry zone)， neck (N34， brainstem and thalamus)， and scalp 通用删除11(英):<u>(P37，primary sensory cortex)</u>.**

【98】**· Abnormalities seen with SSEPs include slowing of the conduction velocities， decreased amplitude， or loss of the potentials. SSEPs are useful in the evaluation of suspected demyelination or myelopathy. 【0】relation between female fetal sex and hyperemesis gravidarum.**

【1】During the third trimester of pregnancy， the gravid uterus can mechanically reduce the distensibility of the stomach as well as change the contour of the cardiac sphincter， leading to an increased inci-dence of vomiting.

【2】Ifvomiting is excessive， develops or persists after14 weeks of gestation and leads to dehydration and/or ketosis， it is called hyperemesis gravi-darum. It affects 1 in 200 pregnant women.，4If vomiting is sustained over a period of time， it will lead to maternal weight loss， oliguria， hypokalaemic alkalosis and constipation. Fetal intrauterine growth restriction is also reported.

【3】In such cases， a pathological cause should be excluded.

【4】The causes of hyperemesis gravidarum are elaborated in Box 1. In a recent study， chronic infection with Helicobacter pylori was present in61.8 per cent of pregnant patients with hyper-emesis in comparison with 27.6 per cent of pregnant patients without hyperemesis. Other studiesShave confirmed1this correlation.b，/A recent study from Turkey has shown higher levels of the hormone leptin in 18 patients with hyperemesis compared to an equal number of healthy pregnant women.

【5】**Differential diagnosis**

【6】Although the potential causes of hyperemesis are many， the most common causes are elabor-ated below.

【7】**Gastrointestinal causes**

【8】The most frequently encountered causes in clinical practice are gastrointestinal in nature. Exclusion of Helicobacter pylori infection is important. In this infection， vomiting may be spontaneous or self-induced for relief of symp-toms， as in peptic ulcer.

【9】Gastroenteritis or food poisoning is com-mon. A variety of pathogens can be involved. The onset of vomiting is abrupt and related to the ingestion of food. Other cases may also be reported after ingestion of the same food. Pre-existing allergies to food products， such as eggs or nuts， can cause intractable vomiting after inadvertent ingestion.

【10】Gallstones may be commonly associated with pregnancy， and can cause both hyperacidity and vomiting. They are easily diagnosed on upper abdominal ultrasound scan. If complicated with cholecystitis， the vomiting will be accompanied with right upper quadrant pain and/or fever.

Inflammation of any part of the gastrointest-inal tract will manifest with vomiting. The most common example is acute appendicitis， when vomiting is accompanied with right iliac fossa pain. Diverticulitis and cholecystitis will also present with vomiting. Acute pancreatitis can|删除1换行|be precipitated by alcohol or may be a compli-cation of underlying gallstones.

【12】Vomiting may be the first symptom in hepa-titis and can precede the appearance of jaundice by a few days. Liver function tests will show ele-vated liver enzymes and hepatitis markers will clinch the diagnosis.

【13】For the other gastrointestinal causes listed in Box 1， there may be a past history of the disease.

【14】Pregnancy-related causes

【15】Multifetal pregnancy  and hydatidiform mole cause hyperemesis in the first trimester and are easily diagnosed on a first trimester scan. Degeneration of coexistent fibroids  with pregnancy will present with vomiting and lower abdominal pain. Ultrasound scans show an increase in size of the fibroid. Management is conservative with rest and analgesics.

【16】Ovarian torsion  can occur with the presence of dermoid cysts of the ovary that can coexist with pregnancy. There is accompanying IoWerabdominal pain and tenderness. Ultrasound scan will show the cyst， while Doppler signals of the ovarian vessels will show impaired flow. Management is surgical with laparoscopic untwisting of the cyst， if diagnosed early. In late cases where gangrene has set in， the ovary may have to be sacrificed.

【17】Pre-eclampsia and the HELLP (haemolysis， elevated liver enzymes and low platelets) syn-drome occur in the third trimester ofpregnancy and are accompanied with raised blood pres-sure and albuminuria. Vomiting may occur because of raised intracranial tension and/or raised liver enzymes， as in the HELLP syndrome.

【20】Acute fatty liver of pregnancy is rare but potentially lethal. Liver enzymes are raised with jaundice. There is hypoglycaemia， hyperuri-caemia， renal impairment， coagulopathy and encephalopathy may ensue.

【21】Acute systemic infections

【22】As part of generalised viraemia or bacteraemia， all acute systemic infections can be accompa-nied with vomiting. In these cases， there are coexistent symptoms of infection， such as fever， body ache， malaise and a raised white cell count.1chorioamnionitis、1uterinecontractions accompany vomiting， which is aggravated due to cervical dilatation.

【23】Central nervous system causes

【24】Raised intracranial tension can be accompanied with vomiting. Benign intracranial hypertension is common in obese young women. It can pres-ent for the first time in pregnancy (in the second trimester) or may worsen if existing prior to pregnancy. Headache and papilloedemaare present without computerised tomography evi-dence of a space-occupying lesion.

【25】Neoplasms can occur rarely in association with pregnancy.

【26】**Middle ear disease**

【27】Middle ear disease can cause vomiting owing to stimulation of the labyrinth. There is often a past history， which is then aggravated in preg-nancy. Motion sickness is common in preg-Ianicys while Meniere'sSdiseasegenerally presents in the fourth decade of life and rarely will coexist with pregnancy. Migraine is often aggravated in pregnancy.

【28】Cardiological causes

【29】Congestive cardiac failure will cause congestion of the liver and hence lead to nausea. In patients with hyperhomocysteinaemia， myocardial infarc-tion may occur at a younger age. If the ischaemia/infarct involves the posterior wall， it irritates the oesophagus and can cause vomiting.

【30】**Endocrinal causes**

【31】Diabetic ketoacidosis may present for the first time in pregnancy with intractable hyperemesis. Blood sugar and urine ketone estimation will clinch the diagnosis. Uraemia， hyperthyroidism andhyperparathyroidism have aal1l1been reported. Addison’s disease will cause infertility in the first instance but de novo deficiency can develop during pregnancy in cases of tubercu-losis of the adrenal gland. Zollinger-Ellison syn-drome leads to increased gastric acid production and vomiting.

【32】Psychological disorders

【33】Both anorexia nervosa and bulimia are com-monly encountered in young girls and pregnancy often aggravates the conditions. Vomiting in these cases may be spontaneous but is often self-induced. Weight loss is usually significant as are nutritional deficiencies. Treatment is by psycho-logical counselling and antidepressants.

【34】Drug-induced/iatrogenic causes

【35】Drugs are mostly avoided during pregnancy； however， some drugs prescribed in pregnancy can cause gastric irritation， e.g.low-dose aspirin pre-scribed for patients with antiphospholipid syn-drome. Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs may also be prescribed for chronic painful conditions such as arthritis. Steroids and amino-phylline may be used for coexisting medical dis-orders and can lead to vomiting. Accidental poisoning with plant derivatives such as ipecac is a rare cailse.

【36】Surgical causes

【37】The most common surgical emergency in preg-nancy is acute appendicitis； however， both diver-ticulitissandccholecystitisSwill present with vomiting. Patients with acute renal or biliary colic vomit as a general response to pain. Intestinal obstruction due to any cause will present with vomiting.

【38】Types of vomiting

【39】The most important clues to diagnosis lie in the history of vomiting anditsaccompanying symptoms.

【40】Vomiting occurring only in the early morning occurs in pregnancy， hyperacidity and uraemia.

【41】Vomiting occurring after food is more likely to point to peptic ulcer， gastroparesis， pyloric obstruction and food poisoning.

【42】Projectile vomiting without nausea occurs in raised intracranial tension. Silent regurgitation of food occurs in oesophageal diverticuli.

【43】Vomiting accompanied by tinnitus and/or giddiness is seen in middle ear disease.

【44】Vomiting accompanied with diarrhoea occurs in enteritis and food poisoning.

【45】Vomiting with chest pain signifies myocardial infarction and， when accompanied with abdominal pain， could signify appendicitis.

【46】Gastrointestinal reflux disease is characterised by reflux of gastric contents during gastric peri-stalsis owing to incompetence of the oesophageal sphincter. In the first trimester， the cause is impaired forward gastric peristalsis， while in the third trimester， the cause could be purely mechanical owing to the gravid uterus pushing up on the stomach. If this becomes a chronic condition， this type of regurgitation will cause damage to the oesophageal lining because of the acidic nature of the contents. In the long run， there is a risk of stricture formation.

【47】**Investigations**

【48】**These should include the following.**

【49】Urine analysis： urine should be checked for specific gravity and the presence of glucose and ketones. It may occasionally show the presence of bile pigments.

【50】Complete blood count： this will show a rise in haematocrit and haemoglobin percentage. There may be slight leucocytosis.

【51】Serum electrolytes， such as sodium and potassium：this will show hyponatraemia， hypokalaemia and， in severe cases， hypokalaemic metabolic acidosis.

【52】Blood sugar hyperglycaemia may be present in diabetes， while hypoglycaemia may be present in per-sistent vomiting， which requires correction with intra-venous fluids.

【53】Liver function tests： 20-30 per cent of women show mild elevation of liver enzymes in hyperemesis. In cases of hepatitis， the enzymes are markedly raised and it may be of value to check the hepatitis mark-ers. Serum amylase and/or lipase will be raised in pancreatitis. Liver function tests also provide an opportunity to look at serum protein levels， an indi-cation of the nutritional status of the mother.

【54】Renal function tests， as renal failure is a complica-tion of severe dehydration.

【55】_Thyroid function fests： 50-70 per cent of women_ have transient hyperthyroidism. This is usually a self-limiting condition and does not require antithyroid therapy.4，12

【56】Parathyroid hormone， if clinically indicated： hyper-parathyroidism is a rare cause of hyperemesis， which may be intractable. High serum calcium levels will point to the diagnosis. Both maternal and fetal morbidity is high and surgery is the definitive cure.3

【57】An electrocardiogram will show widened QRS com-plexes and U waves in hypokalaemia.

【58】An ultrasound scan to confirm intrauterine preg-nancy， to exclude multiple pregnancy or hydatidiform mole. It will also show the presence of gallstones， mesenteric adenitis， dilated loops of bowel in intes-tinal obstruction， the presence of an appendicular lump and small contracted kidneys in uraemia.

【59】**Complications of vomiting**

【60】The most obvious complications are dehydra-tion and malnutrition. Loss of gastric fluid leads todehydration， metabolic alkalo1S _and_ hypokalaemia. The patient will need fluid replacement to treat the dehydration. A general examination will give some idea of the severity of dehydration. The presence of ketones in the urine and a raised haematocrit will confirm the severity of dehydration. The patient then needs to be admitted to hospital.16

【61】The fluid replacement regimen should include fluids， such as normal saline or Hartmann’s solu-tion. Infusion can be started at the rate of100 mL/hour. Potassium chloride should be added to the intravenous infusion according to serum potassium levels. Potassium replacement should be carefully titrated.

【62】Nutritional deficiency should be corrected in consultation with a dietician. Vitamin B1， B6 and B12 deficiency is common and may require sup-plementation. In cases of weight loss and muscle wasting， total parenteral nutrition may be neces-sary. Poor fetal outcomes have been reported if maternal weight loss is >5 per cent in preg-nancy.17 These include fetal intrauterine growth retardation and even fetal death in severe cases.

【63】Other complications of vomiting include the following.

【64】Patients may complain of muscular aches and pains in the intercostal and upper abdominal region due to the accompanying retching.

【65】Constipation， which is common in pregnancy， is aggravated in hyperemesis.

【66】Thrombosis canbe precipitated in ssusceptible patients due to dehydration.

【67】Vomiting may cause tears in the oesophageal epithelium， known as the Mallory-Weiss syndrome， which may result in haematemesis.

【68】Rarely， forceful vomiting will lead to pressure rup-ture of the oesophagus， termed Boerhaave's syn-drome， where the patient will complain of acute severe retrosternal chest pain.

【69】Vomiting during childbirth or under anaesthesia may result in regurgitation of stomach contents into the respiratory passages leading to Mendelson’s syndrome， which requires management in an inten-sive care unit. Subconjunctival haemorrhages may occur， whichhareinconsequential， but retinal detachment can be a serious complication.

【70】Wernicke's encephalopathy has also been reported in continued vomiting and dehydration.18，19 This is due to thiamine (vitamin B1) deficiency， and is charac-terised by diplopia， nystagmus， ataxia and confusion. It can be precipitated by infusion of dextrose-containing fluids. In the presence of Wernicke’s encephalopathy， the incidence of fetal loss is higher.

【71】Erosion of the dentalenamel is seen in the repeated vomiting of bulimia.

【9】**DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS FOR TOXIC ENCEPHALITIS Evaluation**

**As acknowledged by Metter and Bleecker (1994) the “neurological examination by its nature is semiquantitative”. This is particu-larly so when attempting to diagnose a subtle or mild encephalopathy. The ideal strategy for the evaluation of individuals suspected of or claiming neurotoxic exposure is a multidisciplinary approach 删除1:<u>(Hartman，1995)</u>. Potentially this will involve a physician (if possible， a neurolo-gist)， a neuropsychologist， and perhaps an industrial hygienist. In cases of high acute exposure， medical management is primary and neuropsy-chological assessment can be a valuable follow-up procedure to assess|删除1换行|recovery offunction. When the diagnostic issue is one of subclinical effects and/or low-level chronic exposure， then neuropsychological evaluation becomes an important initial contribution to diagnosis and medical man-agement. In cases of suspected dual diagnosis or non-occupational origin(including drug abuse， depression， or workplace stress)， the contribu-tion of the clinical neuropsychologist is important to evaluate affective and neuropsychological status and change from baseline functioning. Further， the neuropsychologist can utilize objective findings and pat-terns of performance to assist when malingering is a consideration.**

【11】**Initial Medical Evaluation**

【12】**Those individuals presenting with suspected toxic exposure should receive a thorough medical and neurological evaluation， with blood or urine toxicology screens for the suspected exposure if the presentation is acute. Alternative medical or neurological illnesses should be ruled out. A particularly useful systematic approach is the Boston University Environmental Neurology Assessment (BUENA) 删除1:<u>(Feldman， 1995)</u> con-tained in Appendix 1. The BUENA approach to investigation can be adjusted appropriately to each potential exposure. Another useful tool may be the Exposure Inventory contained in Appendix 2.**

【13】**If an illness is determined as work related， there are the additional complexities of compensation and job status issues， as well as the potential that other individuals were also exposed (currently or historically). The medica evaluation for encephalitis is determined by the presentation， especially the distinction between acute or chronic encephalitis. Acute encephalopathy from sources other than toxic exposure can often be life threatening， and require immediate diagnosis in order to prevent death or brain damage. In a patient presenting with obvious findings or comtplaints of altered central nervous system function， a complete neu-rologic and mental status exam will detect whether there are any gross central deficits and lateralizing neurologic signs or cerebellar or periph-eral findings that are suggestive of structural disease such as mass lesions or cerebrovascular discase. This initial exam and initial laboratory tests (including as indicated hemoglobin， glucose， oxygen saturation or tension， electrolytes， BUN， calcium， and liver function tests) will assist in deciding whether imaging of the central nervous system for structur-al lesions and/or luinbar puncture for CSF analysis is indicated.**

**Severe acute toxic encephalopathy generally occurs in the absence of anatomic lesions on imaging and in the absence of CSF abnormali-ties. Once competing diagnoses are no longer likely， a more detailed|删除1换行|neuropsychological exam can be helpful in assessing the nature and degree of toxic effect. Clinical features can differ for each type of expo-sure. A familiarity with the potential sources of exposure will be most helpful. Additional domains of inquiry to assist with diagnosis include：**

【15】**_Comprehensive Medical History_**

【16】**The medical history should emphasize other diseases known to cause symptoms of encephalopathy as listed in the section on differential diagnosis. This would also include a comprehensive history of medica-tions (prescription， over-the-counter， and alternative) and substance abuse. Also important is a history of head injury or loss of consciousness.**

【17】**_Occupational and Azocational Interest History_**

【18】**Such a history determines possible exposures， frequency， duration， intervals between exposures， possible interactions with other exposures， or factors from other domains of inquiry. Any social or stress-inducing changes at the worksite should also be queried. A sample exposure inventory is included in Appendix 2.**

【19】**_Exposure Documentation_**

【20】**Specific exposure documentation may be required. In such cases， or when the patient does not initially present with a complaint of exposure but exposure is suspected， the services of an industrial hygienist may be very helpful.**

【21】**_Psychological History_**

【22】**This includes a complete description with functional examples of present symptoms， and a review of other (non-reported) psychomotor symptoms suggestive of depression or anxiety. A comprehensive review of psycho-logical symptoms is important for two reasons. Psychological symptoms are prodromal in many toxic exposures， especially to solvents， and the relationship may be complex 删除1:<u>(Hartman， 1995)</u>. Social relationships(occupational and domestic) and recent life changes are also important to assess.**

【23】**_Family Medical History_**

【24】**Family history inchides causes of death， current illness patterns， and history of other family members/friends with disability. This would help to determine potential underlying sensitivities or diseases that mnay be included in the differential. The family approach to disability is also important to assess and consider.**

【25】**_Baseline Intellectuol and Behavioral Data_**

【26】**Always useful for comparison in neuropsychological examinations， in cases involving potential litigation baseline data is critical to determnine a suspected change from previous levels of functioning. High school and college records are most helpful， but earlier academic records may sometimes be illuminating. Previous work samples and review of the skills required for job performance may also be instructive.**

【27】**_Expanded Mental Status Examination_**

【28】**While the Mini Mental Status Examination (MMSE) can be a screening tool for cognitive deficits， its purpose is to identify gross signs of demen-tia ard not subtle signs of cognitive dysfunction. Thus the absence of negative findings is not an indication of absence of pathology， but impaired performance in any domain warrants further investigation. In the clinical evaluation， there is no substitute for careful observation.As suggested by Armstrong Rahill and Lundberg (1999)， a first question might be whether the patient’s presentation fits with his/her com-plaints. Looking at stature， dress， paraphernalia brought to the office， and the condition of the skin，fingernails， and hair can help to develop a general impression of the individual's approach to self-care. Do you observe fine motor tremor， muscle weakness or poor coordination? Do you notice pauses for word finding or lack of prosodic speech (minimal variation in tone quality during speech)? Does the person follow con-versation well and respond with focused answers? Is there a tangential quality to the language? Does the quality of the answers give evidence of poor problem solving， concrete thinking， or lack of flexibility and deter-mination of alternatives? Does the patient sustain attention throughout the evaluation? Does the speed of responding/mental processing appear about normal? Do the patient's claims of previous functioning levels， now reported as lost， make sense in terms of his/her life history?**

【29】**To screen for signs that co-exist with depression or mood changes， inquire about difficulty sleeping， loss of interest in personal activities， loss of energy， difficulty concentrating， change in appetite/weight， loss of pleasure or personal satisfaction from common daily activities， change in sexual functioning， and suicidal ideation. Listen for com-plaints or anger. Observe for emotional flatness or lability. Does there appear to be more irritability and less self-direction? Mood changes may also be symptoms of some types of exposure.**

【30】**A major diagnostic trigger for potential occupational toxic exposure(even if this is not the presenting complaint) is a patient's report that the symptoms abate during the weekend and thus are less noticeable on**
**Monday (or after two days off) but increase in intensity during the work week. This report， especially if accompanied by changes in mood， affect， or mental efficiency， should warrant further investigation of possible toxic encephalopathy. Referral to a neuropsychologist may be appropri-ate both when findings suggestive of encephalopathy are present， or when symptoms and complaints are not explained by some alternative diagnosis.**

【31】**NEUROPSYCHOLOGICAL EVALUATION**

【32】**Professional Referral**

【33】**When toxin exposure is reported or uncovered as part of the medical history， the neuropsychologist must be aware of the complex and ambiguous diagnosis of subclinical neurotoxic syndromes. If toxins are the likely cause for clients' complaints， it will be important to prevent further exposure and continued neurotoxicity. This recommendation may have serious employment or habitat consequences， but such a determination can be difficult to state with certainty.**

【34】**The role of multiple potential non-occupational risk factors is impor-tant to assess， as well as the role of stress， which may be pre-existing or unrelated， reactive to limitations caused by exposure， or primary as a result of neurotoxicity. In many cases the initial evaluation may contain a high level of ambiguity as differential diagnoses are considered. Serial testing to determine symptom progression may be required to provide a conclusive diagnosis.**

**When accepting the referral， requesting as much information as pos-sible will be heipful， including detailed referral and rule-out questions. Providing copies of medical and academic records will greatly facilitate the speed of record review. Most professionals appreciate an informal telephone conversation prior to assessing complex or sensitive cases. Often， a review of the latest toxicology or occupational literature is help-ful in order to provide the most current research on cognitive areas to assess and to determine the diffcrential patterns of expected neuropsy-chological findings based on both the category of neurotoxin(s) and the specific exposure(s). Neurotoxins have distinctive mechanisms of actions， but most have poorly characterized cognitive effects. However， a pattern of functional specificity has been determined for many neuro-toxicants (e.g.， some may affect motor coordination while some may affect memory) 删除1:<u>(White et al.， 1992)</u>. Neuropsychological assessment of toxic encephalopathy is best developed for exposures to solvents and|删除1换行|lead， but it continues to develop as a field of knowledge. Neuropsycho-logical data is best gathered from case and exposure reports. In some cases it may be necessary to review animal toxicology literature， espe-cially if behavioral tests were done to establish toxicity levels， in order to determine suspected functional systeis to target for assessment.**

【36】**Neuropsychological Assessment**

【37】**The purpose of the clinical neuropsychological examination is to evalu-ate behavior as the product of the nervous system. The neuropsycholog-ical evaluation for suspected toxic encephalopathy should include the following：**

【38】**_A Comblete History， with Review of Medical Records_**

【39】**Collateral information may be requested from family or friends. Academic and performance records or supporting information may be requested to establish pre-morbid functioning ability.**

【40】**_A Diagnostic Interview_**

【41】**The interview considers not only the referral question， but also assesses the potential of other disorders/concurrent psychopathology. The interview process should include a full review of potential symptoms， and may be supplemented with a questionnaire，**

【42】**_Extensive Psychometric Testing_**

【43】**Testing shouild include three dimensions of behavior： (1) cognition (infor-mation handling)， (2) emotionality (feelings and motivation)， and (3) executive function (the organization and expression of behavior) 删除1:<u>(Lezak，1995)</u>. Thus the neuropsychological evaluation has several parts， and generally requires several hours. Mental stamina to sustain this intensive process is itself a diagnostic consideration. Mood and affect at the time of the evaluation are generally reported.**

【82】**HISTORICAL OVERVIEW**

【83】The adrenal gland was described in detail nearly 400 yr ago， but it was Thomas Addison who provided the first concrete evidence of the vital nature of the adrenal glands through an accurate description of the syndrome of adrenocortical insuffi-ciency， termed Addison's disease， in 1855. Since then， numer-ous attempts have been made to characterize the biological or biochemical nature of substances produced and secreted by the adrenal glands mainly through the analysis of an extract from adrenals. Kendall at the Mayo Clinic prepared crystalline cor-tical extracts in 1934， which led to the precise characterization of adrenocortical hormones and their routine use in clinical practice. The successful use of cortisone in treatment of rheuma-toid arthritis in 1949 by Hench and Kendall at the Mayo Clinic further enhanced interest in the clinical application of cortico-steroids. In contrast to these dramatic improvements and suc-cessful use of adrenal corticosteroids， the histopathology of adrenocortical diseases had not necessarily keptpace with these advancements of clinical and/or basic endocrinology. The intro-duction of electron microscopy demonstrated the presence of relatively specific organelles involved in steroidogenesis in adre-nocortical parenchymal cells，including mitochondria with spe-cific cristae and smooth endoplasmic reticulum. However， these findings could not demonstrate the functional localization of corticosteroids， that is， which cell types produce what types of corticosteroids， one of the mostimportantaspects of adrenocor-tical pathology. Introduction of immunohistochemistry yielded remarkable improvements in endocrine pathology in general. Antibodies against corticosteroids that were developed mainly for radioimmunoassay or enzyme-linked immunoassay have been employed in immunohistochemical evaluation of adreno-cortical disorders. However， it was difficult to fix steroids in the tissue and steroids were easily extracted into organic solvents employed in the processofimmunostaining. In addition，immu-noreactivity recognized by antibodies against corticosteroids may represent steroids stored， synthesized， or bound to carrier proteins. Therefore， immunostaining of steroids themselves could not provide any biologically relevant information as to functional pathology.

【86】**THE NORMAL ADRENAL CORTEX**

【87】HISTOLOGYAdrenocortical steroidogenesis is well known to be under the control of the hypothalamo-pituitary-adrenal axis. It is also important to note that the histology of the“nor-mal”human adrenal cortex also changes according to the status of hypothalamo-pituitary-adrenal axis. In the adrenal of nor-mal subjects， three major zones—the zona glomerulosa， zona fasciculate， and zona reticularis—can be appreciated by their histologic structure and their cytologic features 通用删除6(英):<u>\[10\]</u>. The zona glomerulosa is situated around the periphery of the cortex be-neath the capsule and forms rounded nests or clusters of corti-cal cells 通用删除6(英):<u>\[11，12\]</u>. The zona glomerulosa cells are in general small， mitochondria are few in number， and smooth endoplas-mic reticulum is small and relatively not well developed. The zonafasciculatais composed of the clear cortical cells arranged in cords or columnlike fashion. The zona reticularis occupies the inner one third to one quarter of the cortex. Cortical cells of the zona reticularis have eosinophilic compact cytoplasm and are arranged in anastomosing cords 通用删除6(英):<u>\[11，12\]</u>. 【1】慢性淋巴细胞性白血病多见于中老年，起病缓慢，常表现全身淋巴结肿大，以颈、腋下，腹股沟为主。脾轻至中度肿大或肝肿大。白细胞0.02~0.01×10.3°/L，主要为成熟的小淋巴细胞。随病情进展，可有贫血和血小板减少。骨髓增生活跃，成熟淋巴细胞占50%以上，原始及幼稚淋巴细胞<10%。粒系、红系、巨核系减少。正常免疫球蛋白减少，易发生上呼吸道感染和肺炎。

【2】(三)类白血病反应

【3】类白血病反应通常是由于严重感染、恶性肿瘤、药物中毒等刺激造血组织产生的异常反应，表现为外周血中白细胞显著增多，可达5×10×10/L以上，并有幼稚细胞出现。待原因去除后，血象可恢复正常。类白血病反应时，一般无明显贫血和血小板减少；粒细胞有严重毒性改变，胞浆内有毒性颗粒和空泡等，在感染引起时尤为明显；中性粒细胞的碱性磷酸酶活性和糖原皆增高，无 ph 染色体。

【4】四、白细胞功能缺陷

【7】第4节 嗜酸性粒细胞增多症

【8】周围血液中嗜酸性粒细胞绝对值大于0.4×10°/L，称嗜酸性粒细胞增多症(eosinophlia)。嗜酸性粒细胞主要分泌基本蛋白(MBP)，嗜酸性阳离子蛋白(ECP)，嗜酸性衍化中性毒素蛋白(EN())，对寄生虫有杀伤作用。体外实验证实，嗜酸性粒细胞能吞噬微生物及免疫化合物，释放毒性氧化代谢物质，如白介素C，以及血小板活性物质等。嗜酸性粒细胞增多的意义在于：①对寄生虫或其代谢产物具有杀伤细胞的特异性作用；②在超敏反应中作为一种抗炎症调节物质，使某些炎症局限化并防止其扩散；③长期明显的嗜酸粒细胞增多，可引起 Loefiler心内膜炎或局部组织增殖如嗜酸粒细胞肉芽肿。

【9】肠寄生虫感染、药物、食物等引起的变态反应性疾病是嗜酸性粒细胞增多症中最常见的原因。肠寄生虫感染时，幼虫在组织内移行和人侵阶段释放抗原，引起宿主免疫反应，导致嗜酸性粒细胞增多。旦移行终止及发育为成虫，嗜酸粒细胞就可能下降或消失。嗜酸粒细胞通过 Fc 受体附着于抗体 IgG的 Fc 段，经抗体介导细胞依赖的细胞毒作用(AD-CC)，伴有嗜酸性粒细胞的脱颗粒，释出基本蛋白(MBP)和阳离子(ECP)发挥毒性作用。本病患者常有旅行史、饮食史或输血等病史，通过粪便涂片或染色涂片及有关血清学检查如环卵试验等，找到寄生虫感染的证据。

【10】在由药物如阿司匹林、磺胺类等以及一些食物引起的Ⅰ型变态反应性疾病(包括枯草热、过敏性鼻炎、哮喘和湿疹等)，通常伴有嗜酸性粒细胞增多。在I型变态反应中，抗原与肥大细胞表面的 IgE 反应，激活肥大细胞，使之脱颗粒，释放嗜酸性粒细胞趋化因子(ECF-A)，使嗜酸粒细胞聚积于炎症局部，产生多种酶类，对超敏反应起调控作用。

【11】嗜酸粒细胞最引人注目的增多见于嗜酸粒细胞增多症候群，包括 Loefiler 心内膜炎、嗜酸粒细胞白血病和特发性嗜酸粒细胞增多症候群，嗜酸粒细胞计数高达5×10×10°~1000°/L，嗜酸粒细胞增多可能与 IL-5作用有关。IL-5由抗原活化的T细胞分泌，主要生物功能包括：①促进已活化的B淋巴

【12】细胞分化及分泌免疫球蛋白；②诱导 CTL 生成；③诱导人嗜酸性粒细胞的增殖分化及活化。其作用呈剂量依赖性，且能被抗 IL-5抗体特异性中和；④诱导IL-2R 表达。

【13】Loeffer 心内膜炎，又称嗜酸粒细胞增多性心内膜心肌病，以心脏受累为主要表现。心脏呈球形增大，以左侧心脏增大为主。病变组织内发现嗜酸粒细胞，主要由局部沉积的嗜酸粒细胞阳离子蛋白和主要碱性蛋白引起组织损伤。任何一侧心室都可以形成大块附壁血栓，并可能引起心内膜纤维化。由于纤维组织和血栓造成心室腔缩小，导致心室充盈阻力增加即局限性心内膜心肌病。患者有体静脉回流受阻的表现：下垂部位水肿，腹水，肝脏肿大等。心音遥远，可闻及第三、第四心音。此外，血栓形成可致肺栓塞和体循环栓塞，超声心动图见心室尖闭塞，心内膜增厚等有诊断价值的改变。

【14】特发性嗜酸性粒细胞增多症候群代表一组异质性疾病，其共同特点是：外周血嗜酸粒细胞绝对数持续高于1.5×10°/L达半年以上。引起本病的原因不明，有多系统多脏器功能障碍，包括心、中枢神经系统、肾、肺、胃肠道和皮肤，临床表现不一，常有发热、盗汗、咳嗽、胸痛、神经精神症状、瘙痒、皮疹及充血性心力衰竭。最严重的并发症是累及心脏和中枢神经系统，进行性充血性心力衰竭是主要死因之一。

【15】嗜酸性粒细胞性白血病是慢性白血病的临床表现。除发热、贫血、肝脾和淋巴结肿大外，还有突出的心、肺、中枢神经系统和皮肤症状。患者表现心肌损害、心脏扩大、心律不齐、进行性充血性心力衰竭，其他尚有咳嗽、呼吸困难、抽搐、昏迷、皮疹等。外周血检查可有贫血、血小板减少，嗜酸粒细胞增多，可见幼稚嗜酸粒细胞。骨髓增生显著，嗜酸粒细胞明显增多，伴形态异常，可见较多幼稚嗜酸粒细胞。本病可有染色体突变，出现ph 染色体。

【16】除上所述，胶原血管性疾病(如类风湿性关节炎、嗜酸粒细胞性肌膜炎、过敏性血管炎和肉芽肿病)、某些恶性疾病(如 Hodgin's 病、蕈状肉芽肿)以及慢性肉芽肿等疾病，亦可出现嗜酸性粒细胞增多，其机制尚不清楚。

【17】第5节 红细胞增多症

【18】红细胞增多症(erythrocytosis)是指单位体积的外周血液中红细胞计数、血红蛋白量和红细胞比容明显高于同一地区正常数值的一组疾病。在我国平原地区，凡红细胞计数男性≥6.5×10"/L，女性>

【19】6.0×10/L；血红蛋白男性>175g/L，女性>160g/L；红细胞比容，男性>0.54，女性>0.50者即为红细胞增多。

【20】【病因】

【21】(一)绝对性红细胞增多症

【22】1.真性红细胞增多症(真红)。

【23】2.继发性红细胞增多症。

【24】(1)红细胞生成素代偿性红细胞增多症 如新生儿红细胞增多症、高原性红细胞增多症、慢性肺脏疾病、肺换气不良综合征、心血管疾病、动-静脉瘤、血红蛋白病、异常血红素疾病。

【25】(2)非代偿性红细胞增多症 如肾脏疾病(肾脏肿瘤、肾移植、肾囊肿、肾盂积水等)；小脑成血管细胞瘤、肝癌、子宫肌瘤、嗜铬细胞瘤及卵巢癌等。

【26】(二)相对性红细胞增多症

【27】1.失水或休克 各种原因所致体液丢失过多或分布异常，如严重腹泻、呕吐、多汗、高热、大面积烧伤、甲状腺危象、肾上腺危象、糖尿病高渗性昏迷或酮症酸中毒，持续的重症休克，血浆外渗致血容量降低等。

【28】2.假性红细胞增多症 又称应激性红细胞增多症(Gaisboek)综合征，为一种原因不明的慢性相对性红细胞增多。可能与精神紧张、长期吸烟、高血压或过度肥胖有关。

【29】【发病原理】

【30】(一)促红细胞生成素(erythropoietin，EPO)对红细胞生成的调节

【31】EPO是诱导红系祖细胞(CFU-E)分化为原始红细胞所必需的激素，尚可促进血红蛋白合成及幼红细胞成熟，是刺激红细胞生成的主要调节因素。大部分EPO的生成与肾脏密切相关。肝脏及某些肿瘤组织也可少量生成 EPO。EPO 的分泌受组织氧张力高低的调节，氧张力减低则分泌增加，反之则分泌减少。而 EPO量增多时红细胞生成增加，反之则红细胞生成减少。

【32】1\. EPO代偿性增多 继发性红细胞增多系由于各种病因所致的组织缺氧，通过 EPO分泌增多而促使红细胞生成增加。该类疾病主要有：①高原性红细胞增多症，系因高海拔地区大气氧分压低而致机体缺氧；②先天性心脏病有右至左分流或各类心脏病心衰引起组织缺氧；③慢性支气管炎、支气管哮喘、阻塞性肺气肿等多种慢性呼吸道疾病致肺通气与换气功能减弱；④肺外因素如呼吸中枢抑制、呼吸动作的神经、肌肉或胸廓畸形、极度肥胖致机械运动障碍，影响肺的通气与换气；⑤氧亲和力增高的异常

【33】蛋白血症影响氧在组织中的释放。遗传性高铁血红蛋白血症，其血红蛋白缺乏携氧、供氧功能，均可致组织缺氧；⑥长期应用某些药物，如舉丸酮可刺激EPO分泌，钴盐可抑制组织呼吸酶而致组织缺氧，均可引起继发性红细胞增多症。

【34】2\. EPO 非代偿性增多 如肾囊肿、肾盂积水、肾肿瘤等慢性肾脏疾病，某些肿瘤或慢性肝功能减损。机体虽无全身缺氧而可能有肾组织局部缺氧：肝脏对 EPO 清除减少；或肿瘤组织分泌 EPO等，致使血中 EPO水平增高，继发红细胞增多症。

【35】(二)内源性红细胞克隆形成

【36】正常人骨髓细胞体外培养时，需在培养基中加人外源性 EPO才有 CFU-E生长，而真红患者体内有异常红细胞克隆形成，或称内源性红系集落，它对低浓度 EPO 即异常敏感，遂致原发性红细胞增多症。由于这类异常细胞可能在多能干细胞水平即已发生变异，故真红患者的粒系及血小板系也增生过 _多。_

【37】(三)血液浓缩

【38】各种原因所致的体液丢失或分布异常，均可因血浆容量减少而致红细胞计数、血红蛋白浓度及红细胞比容相对增高，而全身红细胞总量并未增加。此种相对性红细胞增多是一过性的，多呈急性经过。慢性相对性红细胞增多症又称假性或应激性红细胞增多症，确切病因与发病机制尚不甚明了。

【39】【诊断方法】

【40】(一)病史

【41】凡持续性红细胞明显增多，长期居住高原地区或有致组织缺氧的原发病者，提示继发性红细胞增多症。中年以后发病，无原发病可寻，要想到真红。有各种失水因素或休克后出现的红细胞增多，当属相对性者。若为血压增高的肥胖嗜烟者，可以发生假性红细胞增多症。

【42】(二)体格检查

【43】失水、休克所致相对性红细胞增多，常有原发病引起的急性病容或特殊表情，皮肤弹性差或皮肤湿冷等。而真红或慢性假性红细胞增多症则皮肤黏膜绛红等多血症表现明显，血压常增高；真红者多有脾肿大，假性红细胞增多症多肥胖。

【44】(三)实验室检查

【45】1.血象 红细胞计数、血红蛋白量及红细胞比容均明显增高，红细胞形态多正常。可见嗜多色红细胞或点彩红细胞，甚至少量有核红细胞等红系增生旺盛表现。网织红细胞正常或轻度增高。真红患

【46】者白细胞计数常中度增高并有核左移，嗜碱粒细胞可以增多，血小板计数也常增高。

【47】2.骨髓象 有核细胞增生明显活跃，以红系增生为主。晚期可伴骨髓纤维化。

【48】3.红细胞容量、血浆容量及总血容量测定 以放射性同位素标记红细胞来测定红细胞容量绝对值，真红和继发性红细胞增多症者均增高，总血容量也增多，但血浆容量正常。相对性者红细胞容量正常，总血容量及血浆容量则减少。

【49】4\. 血浆及尿 EPO测定 真红者明显减低，继发性者增高，而相对性红细胞增多症者则正常。

【50】5.动脉血氧饱和度及氧-血红蛋白解离曲线缺氧性继发性红细胞增多症的动脉血氧饱和度降低，氧解离曲线右移，氧释放增加。继发于异常血红蛋白血症者，其血氧饱和度正常或增高，氧解度曲线左移，氧释放减少。

【51】6.红系祖细胞体外培养 真红可见内源性红系集落生长。

【52】7.血红蛋白淀粉凝胶或等电焦聚电泳 有助于氧亲和力增高的异常血红蛋白病的诊断。

【53】8.其他测定 真红患者的中性粒细胞碱性磷酸酶活性(NAP)、血组织胺测定、血及尿的尿酸测定及血清维生素B常有增高。部分真红患者可有染色体核型异常。

【54】(四)仪器检查

【55】必要时，可作心脏、肾脏、脾脏等部位的超声波、CT、静脉肾盂造影、胸部X线或肺功能等检查。

【56】【鉴别诊断】 因失水以及重症休克所致的暂时性红细胞增多症，由于持续性呕吐、腹泻、高热、多汗、烧伤、甲亢、重症糖尿病等可引起血浆容量丢失而使血液浓缩的原因显而易见，休克的存在也不易被忽略，故而其诊断不难。呈慢性经过的真性红细胞增多症、假性红细胞增多症以及各种原因所致的继发性红细胞增多症则应注意鉴别。

【57】(一)真性红细胞增多症

【58】真红是一种原因未明的骨髓发育异常性疾病。其临床特点为起病缓慢、病程较长，红细胞明显增多，全血容量增加，常伴有白细胞与血小板增多，皮肤黏膜绛红，脾脏肿大，部分患者常有出血、皮肤瘙痒、腹胀及各部位血管栓塞症状。典型者根据皮肤暗红、脾大及全血细胞增多三大表现，伴有血氧饱和度正常，诊断不难。真红与继发性及假性红细胞增多症的鉴别要点见表11-1。

【61】(二)假性红细胞增多症

【62】本症又称应激性红细胞增多症或 Gaisbock 综合征，病因未明。其特点是患者常较肥胖，有神经质，高血压，但肝脾不大。外周血红细胞比容增高而红细胞总容量正常，血浆容量减少，白细胞及血小板计数正常，与真红不同。

【63】(三)继发性红细胞增多症

【64】1.高原性红细胞增多症 患者长期居留于高海拔地区，有多血症表现，可与高血压及或心脏病等其他高原反应表现同时存在。一般无脾肿大，白细胞、血小板计数一般正常。

【65】2.原发性肺动脉高压症 本症又称 Ayerza 综合征。其主要病理改变为肺动脉及其分支的硬化，有的是肺动脉先天性狭窄或发育不全，致使肺动脉压异常增高。临床特点为慢性进行性加重的呼吸困难，常有晕厥、咯血、紫绀，逐渐出现右心室肥厚、扩张及慢性充血性心衰。于胸骨左缘第二、三肋间可闻及收缩期杂音及第二心音亢进与分裂。胸部X线片示肺动脉扩张，肺内却呈少血征。心导管及心血管造影示肺动脉压力增高，造影剂进人左房时间延迟。其他有肺动脉高压的疾病，如风湿性心脏病二尖瓣病变，先天性动脉导管未闭与间隔缺损，根据病史、心脏杂音，X线有肺内充血征；慢性肺源性心脏病之病史与肺气肿体征，可资与本病鉴别。

【66】3.肺换气不良综合征 本病又称 Pickwickian综合征。可由慢性支气管、肺疾患引起，或因中枢或周围性神经系统异常引起呼吸肌运动障碍，致肺泡通气与换气功能减低引起缺氧，出现头晕、嗜睡和扑翼样震颤等。血 pH值减低，血氧饱和度减低，二氧化碳分压增高或正常。根据病史及原发基础疾患表

【67】现有助鉴别。

【68】4.血红蛋白病 机体存在与氧亲和力增加的血红蛋白，患者血氧饱和度虽然正常，但组织缺氧， EPO生成增加，致红细胞增多。血红蛋白电泳有助诊断。

【69】5.遗传性高铁血红蛋白血症 因患者红细胞内缺乏高铁血红蛋白还原酶所致。皮肤呈棕褐色紫绀，吸氧不能改善，无心肺疾患。根据病史及化验，不难确诊。

【70】6.肾脏疾病在除外缺氧所致 EPO代偿性红细胞增多症之后，即应想到肾脏疾病所致者。通过影像学检查及相关实验室检查，对肾癌、多囊肾、肾盂积水、肾良性腺瘤、肾肉瘤、肾结核和继发性肾肿瘤等可以引起继发性红细胞增多症的肾脏疾病的诊断很有帮助。

【71】第6节高高丙种球蛋白血症

【72】临床上许多疾病可引起高丙种球蛋白血症(hy-pergamma globinemia，HGG)，它是由于免疫系统受多种外界抗原或内在因素的刺激引起的一种免疫应答反应，经B淋巴细胞增生、分化，主要在浆细胞内合成和分泌丙种球蛋白增加，使血液中丙种球蛋白增高，因丙种球蛋白大多属于免疫球蛋白(immuno-globulin，简称 Ig)，具有抗体活性，因而 HGG称为高免疫球蛋白血症(hyperimmunoglobulinema，HIG)。高丙种球蛋白血症可分为如下两种：

【73】1.多克隆丙种球蛋白血症(多克隆HGG)或多克隆免疫球蛋白血症(多克隆HIG)，系由来自不同浆细胞系(或克隆)增生而产生的不同类型的 Ig的

【74】增多，如 IgG、AIgA及IgM等。

【75】2.单克隆高丙种球蛋白血症(单克隆HGG)，或单克隆高免疫球蛋白血症(单克隆HIG)，为由单一种浆细胞克隆增生产生的一种类型 Ig 的增多，可为 IgG，亦可为 IgM或 IgA。这种Ig常为异常 Ig或其片段，大多不能检出抗体活性，故此类 Ig又称副蛋白(paraprotein)或 M 蛋白(M-protein)。多克隆HGG 主要常于感染、炎症和免疫性疾病，属良性HGG，然而有少数也见于恶性淋巴瘤细胞增生性疾病；而单克隆 HGG 大多见于恶性浆细胞疾病，也可见于淋巴细胞恶性增生性疾病或癌前病变。因此，两种病变的鉴别具有重要的临床意义。本节重点叙述单克隆高丙种球蛋白血症。

【76】【发病原理】 免疫球蛋白是人体受抗原刺激后所产生的具有抗体作用的一类球蛋白。正常Ig 根据其理化性质，尤其是免疫性能可分为五大类及其亚型通用删除1(中):<u>(表11-2)</u>。这五类分别为 IgG、IgA、IgM、IgD及IgE，各种 Ig都具有共同的基本结构单位，即四链单位。他们是由两条相同的长多肽链(又称重链或H链)和两条相同的短多肽链(又称轻链或L链)

【77】组成，四条多肽链又借助二硫键构成四链单位。重链占整个Ig分子的2/3，轻链占1/3。链的一端为氨基端，另一端为羧基端。不管轻链或重链都有两个相同部位，即近氨基端的可变区(V区)的近羧基端的不变区(C区)，可变区是抗原与 Ig结合的部位。依据不变区的抗原特异性，可将轻链分为两型，分别以希腊字母i(kappa)和A(lambda)来表示，即x链和入链。重链可分为五大类，分别以希腊字母Y(gam-ma)、a(alpha)、p(mp)、8(delta)、e(epsilon)表示，它们决定 Ig 的特性，含有相应重链的 Ig 依次为 IgG、IgA、IgM、IgD和 IgE。 Ig 主要由浆细胞合成，每种浆细胞系只能产生一种Ig，不同类型的Ig是由不同解剖部位与组织中的浆细胞合成。如 IgG 主要由脾脏及周围淋巴结中的浆细胞合成，而合成 IgA 的浆细胞主要在呼吸道及消化道的黏膜固有层，以后者更为重要。IgM 合成的部位可能在淋巴细胞或浆细胞。IgE 主要由扁桃体及呼吸道和消化道黏膜固有层中的浆细胞合成。因此，不同抗原的刺激能诱导特定的浆细胞系产生不同类型的Ig。

【80】多克隆 HGG 在临床上较为常见，在多数情况下3种主要 Ig(IgG、IgA、IgM)不同程度增多，但在少数情况下仅一种Ig增多。根据病因不同，血液中多种 Ig 增多所经历时间可较短暂，如由感染引起者，当感染被控制后，血液中Ig即可逐渐恢复正常；但也可呈持续性增高，如见于系统性红斑狼疮、慢性活动性肝炎等一类不能完全治愈的疾病。单克隆HGG 主要出现于多发性骨髓瘤、巨球蛋白血症，这种肿瘤性 Ig 增多不同于正常的Ig，除不具有抗体活性外，而且还能引起病理效应。恶性增生的浆细胞因其合成 Ig 功能障碍，合成重链和轻链的量有时并

【81】不成正常比例，而往往合成轻链过多，所以血液中除出现单一Ig外，有时还河出现游离的轻链，由于轻链的相对分子质量较小，常可随尿排出，此即为凝溶蛋白(即 Bence Jonce 蛋白，BJ蛋白)。如BJ蛋白呈单独出现，并不伴有任何一种Ig增多，称为轻链病(rc或入型)。若血和尿中出现过多重链或其片段，而非 Ig增高，称为重链病，现已发现有丫链、链和p链三型重链病，少数病人还可出现7sIgM，半分子IgG 及半分子 IgA等。

【82】恶性单克隆 Ig增多的病因和发病机制目前尚未完全阐明。根据动物实验和临床观察，放射、化学

【83】品(苯、石棉)、抗原对网状内皮系统的反复刺激、EB病毒感染以及遗传因素等都可引起恶性单克隆 Ig增多。Radl 等发现在CBL/KalwRij 小鼠存在与人类相同的单克隆丙种球蛋白病(monoclonal gam-mopathies，MG)，患 MG 老龄小鼠的骨髓和脾细胞可移植给年轻小鼠。他们将 C，gBL小鼠的胸腺切除后，小鼠的 MG 发病率明显增多。这些现象提示M蛋白的发生与：①T淋巴细胞功能的损害；②缺少T淋巴细胞对B淋巴细胞的抑制；③一种自发的或病毒诱导基因突变引起B淋巴细胞的单克隆增生有关。近年来，人们应用单克隆抗体检测方法，发现人骨髓瘤患者有T淋巴细胞亚群分布异常，表现在T细胞减少，而T：细胞增多，T./T：比值降低，提示患者存在免疫调节细胞紊乱，但这究竟属 MG的病因，还是 MG 所致继发改变，目前尚不十分清楚。有人认为T抑制细胞增加抑制了正常多克隆 Ig 的：合成，而M蛋白则有对抗T抑制细胞的作用，因而产生MG，这种假说尚待证实。近来经实验还发现B淋巴细胞的异常与MG的发病有关，骨髓瘤患者的周围G淋巴细胞亚群表达与骨髓瘤细胞具有相同的基因型和相同的克隆基因重排现象。通过免疫表型和流式细胞仪检查，这种B细胞亚群属于前B骨髓瘤细胞。正常B细胞的分化增生需依赖某些淋巴生长因子。静止B淋巴细胞进人DNA合成期需要白介素-4(IL-4)，细胞增生则需 IL-5，最后通过IL-6的作用促使B淋巴细胞分化成浆细胞。IL-6是骨髓瘤细胞生长的重要因子，患者的血液中IL-6水平升高。Kawano 等人从骨髓瘤患者分离出骨髓瘤细胞，发现瘤细胞能产生B淋巴细胞刺激因子(BSF)-2(IL-6)，以及表达出其受体。同样EB病毒阴性的人骨髓瘤细胞系能产生B淋巴细胞生长因子(IL-5)。这些结果提示骨髓瘤发生存在着一种自身促进途径。

【84】晚近，通过细胞遗传学和分子生物学的研究，发现约半数骨髓瘤患者有染色体异常，表现为非整倍体、多倍体、三体3、5、9、15和单体13、16，并有染色体转位t(8；14)(q24；q32)和t(11；14)(q13；q32)。已知 8q24 和 11q13 是原癌基因 c-myc 和 Bcl-1 部位，而 14q32 是 Ig重链基因位点，这种转位如淋巴瘤发病一样，致使这些基因的转录失去调节，随后使B淋巴细胞向恶性转变而引起骨髓瘤。此外，也发现c-myc 和 H-ras 基因表达异常，c-myc 信息 RNA(mRNA)水平增加，多数病人有 Ig 重链和轻链基因的重排，非整倍体瘤细胞出现高 H-rasP21 蛋白荧光，而 H-ras 基因也位于11对染色体上。因此，H-

【85】ras 和 c-myc 基因表达异常对骨髓瘤的发病也起到重要作用。总之，有关恶性单克隆MG的发病机制尚待进一步加以阐明。

【90】(2)螺旋体感染 钩端螺旋体病、梅毒。

【91】(3)病毒感染 病毒性肝炎、传染性单核细胞增多症、淋巴肉芽肿。

【92】(4)立克次体感染 斑疹伤寒。

【93】(5)原虫感染 疟疾、锥虫病、黑热病。

【94】(6)蠕虫感染 毛线虫病。

【95】(7)真菌感染 多见于深部真菌感染。

【96】2.肉芽肿病 结节病、慢性铍中毒。

【97】3.肝脏疾病 慢性活动性肝炎、病毒性肝炎、小结节性肝硬化、胆汁性肝硬化。

【108】(7)癌肿中 多见于肠、肺、胆道、乳腺及前列腺。

【109】2.良性单克隆丙种球蛋白病** **意义未明的单克隆丙种球蛋白病(monoclonal gammopathies of un-determind significance，MGUS)：良性、伴有产生单克隆蛋白的未知细胞型肿瘤、双克隆丙种球蛋白病。

【110】继发性：感染、自身免疫性疾病、肝脏疾病、某些皮肤病。

【111】【诊断方法】

【112】(一)病史

【113】轻度 HGG一般都无明显自觉症状，不被患者所察觉。当血浆异常丙种球蛋白明显增高(>30g/L)而引起血液黏滞度显著增加时，患者可出现乏力、头痛、眩晕、嗜睡、皮肤黏膜出血、视力障碍，严重时可发生瘫痪、癫痫，甚至昏迷，即为高黏滞综合征。如患者，尤其是老年患者出现不明原因的上述表现，应怀疑有 HGG。临床上明显 HGG大多见于肿瘤性单克隆丙种球蛋白增多，应重点询问有无骨骼疼痛、贫血、出血、肾功能不良表现及反复感染史，特别是呼吸道和皮肤感染。对有慢性感染、肝脏疾病、自身免疫性疾病等有关病史者，应考虑为多克隆性HGG或良性单克隆 HGG。老年人长期无明确症状而血液中丙种球蛋白明显增高者应疑为 MGUS。

【114】(二)体格检查

【115】应重点检查皮肤黏膜有无苍白、出血、黄疸、骨骼压痛和畸形、淋巴结及肝脾肿大程度和硬度。眼底检查观察有无渗出、出血和静脉曲张。有无上述异常体征存在，对于 HGG的性质和病因都有一定帮助。

【116】此外，还应注意某些体征与环境温度的关系，如伴有冷球蛋白血症的患者，在寒冷时常可出现Raynaud 现象，表现远端肢体发冷、发绀，甚至出现坏死。

【117】(三)实验室检查

【118】1.血液学检查 除血常规检查以了解有无贫血存在及贫血程度、白细胞、血小板计数是否增高域减少外，重点是血涂片观察，其内容包括：①红细胞有无缗钱状形成；②有无异常浆细胞或淋巴细胞出现。红细胞呈缗钱状排列，提示有 HGG；如发现少量幼稚浆细胞(一般低于2%)，应考虑多发性骨髓瘤，若浆细胞超过20%且大多为幼稚型则可诊断为浆细胞白血病。出现较多异常淋巴细胞者，应考虑为良性或恶性淋巴细胞增生性疾病。白细胞和血小板计数在疾病早期一般在正常范围，当疾病进展到后期时，由于骨髓被肿瘤细胞浸润，两者可以减少，并伴有严重贫血。

【119】2.骨髓检查 单克隆 HGG 患者应进行骨髓检查，常可协助病因的诊断。多发性骨髓瘤患者的骨髓涂片中可见幼稚型浆细胞明显增多，一般在10%~30%以上。如骨髓中浆细胞轻度增高(<10%)且多数为成熟型，则可能为反应性浆细胞增多，如慢性感染、肝脏疾病、自身免疫性疾病及某些癌肿移植。骨髓有较多淋巴样浆细胞时，可见于巨球蛋白血症患者。异常淋巴细胞明显增多应考虑恶性淋巴瘤、

【120】淋巴细胞白血病，病毒感染。

【121】3.血清蛋白的检查

【122】(1)血清总蛋白量 在多发性骨瘤、巨球蛋白血症约80%以上患者的血清总蛋白量明显增高，以巨球蛋白血症更为明显。多克隆 HGG 患者的血清总蛋白量呈轻、中度增高。轻链病、重链病、淀粉样变及IgD型骨髓瘤患者血清总蛋白量可不增高。当患者并发严重肝脏和肾脏病时，血清总蛋白量可因合成减少或排泄过多而降低。

【123】(2)醋酸纤维薄膜电泳 可将血清蛋白成分分为5条带，经光密度计扫描检出各带的波峰。Ig主要在β和y部分，多克隆 HGG其Y区带可见宽高波峰；而单克隆 HGG在y区或p-y区间可见一条高而狭窄均一的波峰，即M蛋白或M成分(M-compo-nent)。这种M蛋白往往是病理性蛋白，常见于多发性骨髓瘤、巨球蛋白血症，是发现M蛋白的最简便有效的一种初筛检查方法。但 IgD型骨髓瘤、轻链病和重链病的副蛋白可无M波峰或不明显，偶尔呈宽波峰，常被误诊为多克隆丙种球蛋白增多。因此，这类病人应进一步作免疫电泳加以明确。

【124】(3)免疫电泳 M蛋白免疫电泳检查是基于M蛋白为单克隆性 Ig，其结构及理化性质具有同质性。因此，通过免疫电泳方法，特殊抗血清与患者血清中的相应抗体结合从而形成大小和深浅不同的沉淀弧。据此以确定M蛋白的类型与亚型通用删除1(中):<u>(表11-3)</u>，已成为临床鉴定M蛋白成分的一种重要方法。

【137】4.尿检查

【138】(1) 尿 Bence Jones(BJ)蛋白检查 将尿在酸性条件(pH5.0)下加热至50℃~60℃，出现混浊并有白色沉淀，再加热到90℃~100℃，沉淀物又复溶解，表示有BJ蛋白存在。B蛋白实际是 Ig 的轻链(k或A)，其阳性反应大多见于多发性骨髓瘤、原发性巨球蛋白血症、轻链病，有时在 SLE 或肝病时也可呈阳性反应，但其属于多克隆轻链。该方法测定尿BJ蛋白并不敏感，如尿液中BJ蛋白<1mg/ml，则呈阴性反应。可用浓缩20~3000倍尿以提高BJ蛋白的检出率。也可采用磺水杨酸(SSA)试验测定BJ蛋白，此法比加热法敏感，尿液 BJ蛋白浓度0.1mg/ml时，此法可呈阳性。但 SSA 法也能使白蛋白沉淀，特异性不强。若尿 SSA 法阳性，再用浸渍法(dipstick)测尿蛋白质，如为阴性，则很可能为BJ蛋白。有时BJ蛋白呈间歇性出现，故需反复进行尿BJ蛋白的检查。

【139】(2)浓缩尿蛋白电泳 如在a、或y区带出现狭窄高峰，提示有BJ蛋白存在，应进一步用免疫电泳分析以鉴定r链还是入链。如病变累及肾脏时，则尿蛋白电泳可出现类似血清蛋白电泳的图谱。

【140】下观察，刚果红能产生苹果绿颜色的双折射。如刚果红染色阴性，则需进行电镜检查，如有淀粉样变存在，可见长度不等、中空无分支的微纤丝。病变骨骼及内脏组织病理学检查也是诊断髓外浆细胞瘤的重要方法。

【141】6.骨骼X线检查骨骼尤其是颅骨、骨盆、脊椎和肋骨等部位如见到大小不等的圆形骨质破坏区呈“凿孔状"损害，提示为多发性骨髓瘤，有时还可见到病理性骨折、骨质疏松表现。在其他恶性单克隆HGG则很少有骨质破坏。因此，X线检查有助于骨髓瘤的诊断。

【142】7.其他检查①血沉常明显增快；②肾功能检查：骨髓瘤和巨球蛋白血症患者常显示有肾功能减退，尤其是伴有轻链尿患者，故对判断疾病的预后有重要价值；③血清钙检查：发现血钙增高见于骨髓瘤有骨质破坏的患者，如血钙持续增高，表示预后不良；④血清碱性磷酸酶测定：在骨髓瘤往往无增高，主要因骨髓瘤的病变引起骨质破坏，但无成骨过程。这与骨骼转移癌有血清碱性磷酸酶明显增高可资鉴别；⑤血液黏度测定：在正常人血浆比黏度约为1.5~1.7，如比黏度超过5时，可出现高黏滞综合征。

【143】【鉴别诊断】

【144】(一)多发性骨髓瘤(MM，或称浆细胞骨髓瘤)

【145】是一种常见的骨髓浆细胞恶性增生性疾病。大多在50岁以后发病，男性多于女性。疾病早期或隐定型患者可无明显症状，活动期(进展期)可出现骨骼疼痛、贫血及肾功能减退等表现。典型多发性骨髓瘤的诊断并无困难。根据：①骨骼疼痛，典型的溶骨性损害；②血清蛋白电泳出现M蛋白，血清Ig含量IgG≥35g/L、IgA>20g/L、IgD>2.0g/L、IgE>2.0g/L、IgM>15g/L；③骨髓中幼稚浆细胞>10%，或其他组织中有异常浆细胞浸润即可作出诊断。不典型病例则需与诸如结缔组织病、淋巴肿瘤、肝病、癌肿及自身免疫性疾病所致反应性浆细胞增多和Ig增多鉴别。后者骨髓浆细胞数一般<10%，大多数为成熟浆细胞，血清为轻度多克隆 Ig 增高，一般无M蛋白，结合有原发疾病的临床表现和相关检查易于鉴别。稳定性多发性骨髓瘤又称潜伏型多发性骨髓瘤(smoldering multiple myeloma，SMM)，临床可较长时期不出现任何症状，而血清丙种球蛋白明显增高，有M蛋白，此型多发性骨髓瘤需与 MGUS或良性单克隆MG相区别通用删除1(中):<u>(表11-6)</u>。但在长期随访中，约有 10%的 MGUS 患者可发展为恶性浆细胞疾病。因此，对于初诊为 MGUS 者，必须定期随访血清M蛋白的改变。

【157】(二)原发性巨球蛋白血症

【158】本症是B淋巴细胞呈恶性增生，19sIgM大量增多的一种单克隆 HGG。好发于50~60岁以上男性，起病缓慢，疾病早期表现为乏力、软弱、倦怠、头痛，1/3患者有视力障碍，多数患者有眼底静脉淤血、迂曲、扩张呈节段性改变，视网膜有水肿、出血及渗出物。本病是高黏滞血症的主要原因，患者有眩晕、头晕、眼球震颤、麻木、嗜睡、意识障碍、一过性瘫痪、昏迷等表现。神经系病变包括弥漫性脑病、周围神经炎、X线检查一般少见溶骨性病变征象。血沉增快显著，血浆黏滞度增高，常可高达10以上。本病诊断依据：①血清中 19sIgM>10g/L；②骨髓中淋巴样细胞或淋巴样浆细胞显著增高，而不典型浆细胞一般不超过5%。本病主要需与多发性骨髓瘤、伴有 IgM增高的淋巴瘤及 IgM型 MGUS鉴别通用删除1(中):<u>(表11-7)</u>。

【161】(三)重链病(HCD)

【162】为浆细胞或淋巴细胞恶性增生性疾病，其产生的单克隆 Ig仅为多肽重链，而无轻链合成。迄今仅发现y、a、u、8四种重链病，其中8型甚少见。本病临床表现类似淋巴瘤，患者有乏力、贫血、发热、淋巴结及肝脾肿大。但其诊断主要需依赖免疫电泳检测出血清和尿液中有重链，而无轻链。但某些重链病在常规免疫电泳中有时不一定出现沉淀带，临床上疑为重链病的患者，其血清还需采用单个特异的抗a、抗y、抗p重链的抗血清来检查。几种重链病的临床与实验室检查发现不尽相同。

【0】mass may be palpable in the upper abdomen in early stages. Rectal examination may show a cervix-like mass and blood on the examining finger. Plain X-ray abdomen may reveal absence of bowel gas in the right lower quadrant and dilated loops of small bowel.

【1】**Abdominal Pain**

【2】Barium enema may reveal the intussusception as an inverted cap and an obstruction to the progression of barium. In the area of intussusception， there may be a ceiling-spring appearance to the column of barium. _Conservative hydrostatic reductionn gives good results_ 1inan overwhelming majority of the patients. It should be avoided in the presence of strangulation， perforation， or severe toxicity.

【3】Surgical reduction may become necessary in some cases.

【4】**Acute Gastritis**

【5】In acute gastritis， regardless of origin， epigastric pain， tenderness and sensation of pressure and fullness， especially intensifying after food consumption， occur. Nausea， vomiting， belching and lack of appetite are other symptoms.

【6】**Viral Hepatitis**

【7】Nonspecific pain， localized in the right upper quadrant， may occur in some children at the onset of viral hepatitis. Accompanying features include anorexia， jaundice， tender hepatomegaly， and fatty food intol-erance. If jaundice is yet to make its appearance but diagnosis of hepatitis is suspected， you must test urine for bile salts and pigments followed by other liver function test， if necessary.

【8】**Liver Abscess**

【9】Besides pain in the right hypochondrium (often referred to the right shoulder)， the patient is febrile. The liver is enlarged and tender.

【10】Screening shows raised and immobile diaphragm. Demonstration of E. histolytica in stool and aspiration of characteristic anchovy\*sauce (chocolate colored) pus from liver swelling establishes the diagnosis of amebic liver abscess.

【11】**Subphrenic Abscess**

【12】Subphrenic abscess of whatsoever origin (usually it is bursting of a liver abscess， appendicitis， colitis) causes pain

【33】**HISTORY**

【34】In the majority， facial pain originates from local structures. Therefore when formulating a differential diagnosis， consider the conditions affecting the anatomical structures of the face.

【35】**Site**

【36】The site of pain is perhaps the most useful feature when discriminating between the causes. Although local tenderness may direct the clinician to the affected site， do not forget to consider referred pain from adjacent structures. Pain in the region of the ear may be referred from the skin， teeth， tonsils， pharynx， larynx or neck. Tenderness over the maxilla may be due to sinusitis， dental abscess or carcinoma.

【37】Patients with trigeminal neuralgia often describe paroxysms of sharp， severe pains in the distribution of the trigeminal nerve or major divisions. Pain associated with infections of structures such as the teeth， mastoid and ear often has a dull， aching quality.

【38】**Precipitating factors**

【39】Pain precipitated by food or chewing action may be due to a dental abscess， salivary gland disorder， salivary duct disorder， temporomandibular joint disorder or jaw claudication due to temporal arteritis. Pain arising from most structures is aggravated by touch； however， with trigeminal neuralgia， even the slightest stroking of the skin is sufficient to produce intense pain (allodynia).

【40】**Associated symptoms**

【41】Tears may result when the lacrimal duct is obstructed by nasopharyngeal carcinoma. Complaints of otorrhoea and hearing loss should direct the clinician to infections affecting the ear or mastoid. Nasal obstruction and rhinorrhoea occur with maxillary sinusitis and carcinoma of the maxillary antrum. These may be accompanied by unilateral epistaxis. Swelling of the cheek may be experienced with dental abscesses and maxillary carcinoma. Proximal muscle pain， stiffness and subjective weakness may accompany temporal arteritis due to associated polymyalgia rheumatica. Paraesthesia in the distribution of the trigeminal nerve often precedes the rash of herpes zoster.

【42】**EXAMINATION**

【43】**Inspection**

【44】A thorough inspection of the face， salivary glands， ear， nose and throat may produce a wealth of information. This involves the use of specific equipment， such as the otoscope and nasal speculum. Unilateral erythema and vesicles in the distribution of the trigeminal nerve may be striking with herpes zoster infection but may not be present in the early stages of the disease. Localised areas of erythema or swelling may also correspond to the site of infection， such as the sinus， ear， mastoid and parotid gland. Post-auricular swelling and downward displacement of the pinna may be observed with mastoiditis. Maxillary swelling and erythema can be caused by dental abscess or maxillary carcinoma. With otitis media， injection or perforation of the tympanic membrane may be visualised with an otoscope. Nasopharyngeal carcinoma may be seen on direct inspection of the nose and throat. Facial paralysis may be seen with infiltration of the facial nerve by tumours of the parotid gland.

【45】Gentle stroking of the skin of the face will precipitate severe pain with trigeminal neuralgia. Tenderness may be elicited over the frontal bone with frontal sinusitis， and over the maxilla with maxillary sinusitis. With dental abscesses， pain is elicited over the maxilla or mandible. Mastoid tenderness occurs with mastoiditis or otitis media， and parotid tenderness can result from either mumps or parotitis. Tenderness along the course of the superficial temporal artery is suggestive of temporal arteritis. Movement of the pinna produces pain with otitis externa.

【46】Palpation of the superficial lymph nodes of the neck may reveal lymphadenopathy in the distribution of the lymph drainage of structures affected by infection or carcinoma.

【90】**Traumatic**

【91】Usually obvious history of trauma. Swelling may be severe， with bruising and closure of the palpebral fissures. Insect bites may cause swelling due to allergy or infection. The patient may not be aware of an insect bite.

【92】Erysipelas is an uncommon skin infection caused by streptococci. Pain and redness are apparent usually over the cheek. Pyrexia and malaise may occur. Dental infections are common  and are often initially localised， but the side of the face may swell. There is severe associated throbbing pain. Sinusitis presents with constant unilateral pain over the frontal or maxillary sinuses. There is usually puffiness of the skin overlying the sinus. Parotitis presents with pain and swelling over the gland. If this is due to obstruction in the duct， the swelling occurs during eating， when the patient salivates， and regresses afterwards. Bilateral parotitis occurs with mumps.

Congenital hypothyroidism (formerly known as cretinism) is associated with a puffy swollen face and enlargement and protrusion of the tongue. Gross acquired clinical hypothyroidism produces characteristic non-pitting oedematous changes in the skin of the face， giving rise to a characteristic clinical appearance.

【105】**Traumatic**

【106】Fractures are usually obvious. Check pupillary reaction and test the cranial nerves. Insect-bite puncture wounds may be obvious but often they are not. There is often surrounding cellulitis and oedema.

【107】Erysipelas presents as a red， tender area with well-demarcated margins raised above the surrounding normal skin. The patient is usually pyrexial. 【111】In Cushing's syndrome， there will be moon face， and usually other features such as striae， buffalo hump， proximal myopathy. In congenital hypothyroidism， there is a broad， flat face， the eyes are wide apart and the tongue protrudes from the mouth. In acromegaly， there is a large face with overgrowth of the soft tissues of the face， nose， lips and tongue. The patient will have large hands and a large protuberant jaw (prognathism).

【112】In renal failure， the swelling usually occurs around the eyes. There may also be peripheral oedema and hypertension. There is usually a bronze-lemon tinge to the skin in chronic renal failure.

In Paget’s disease， there is an enlargement of the skull， with the vault of the skull bulging outwards above the eyes. Deafness may occur. Occasionally， there is compression of the cranial nerves.
