【1】If a client is displaying the symptoms characteristic of schizophrenia and the time frame since initial display of symptoms is between 1 and 6 months(and symptoms are not due to another condition) the appropriate diagnosis is Schizophreniform Disorder 删除1:<u>(APA， 2013)</u>. To a large extent， this particular di-agnosis exists to ensure that the label of schizophrenia is not used too quickly. Because the psychosocial impairment associated with schizophrenia develops and usually intensifies over time， clients with Schizophreniform Disorder may not present with marked psychosocial problems or decline in functioning.

【2】The diversity of symptoms in schizophrenia is well recognized， as is the associ-ated devastation in personal， vocational， and social relationships. Not surprisingly， an individual with such symptoms experiences significant psychosocial impair-ment and/or distress.Schizophrenia may manifest as severe disruptions in thinking， gross disorganization in thoughts， or may involve delusions (i.e.， systems of false beliefs that vary in elaborateness but are not open to reason or appeal). The client may experience severe perceptual disturbances such as hallucinations (i.e.， sensory experiences in the absence of sensory input). The most common hallucinatory ex-periences are auditory， in which the client hears one or more voices in much the same manner， as he or she would hear someone else talking. The remaining symp toms are sometimes labeled “negative”in that they represent the relative absence of things like affect， motivation， and/or interaction 删除1:<u>(APA， 2013)</u>.

【3】For a diagnosis of schizophrenia， two or more“active-phase”symptoms must occur for a majority of a one-month period (unless responding positively to treatment) with the distress lasting at least 6 months. With modern treatment， it is unlikely that a single episode would encompass this entire time framework. Symptoms include：delusions (i.e.，systems offalsebeliefs that vary inelaborateness but are not open to reason or appeal)； hallucinations (i.e.， sensory experiences in the absence of sensory input)； “disorganized thinking/speech (i.e.， frequent derailment or incoherence)； grossly disorganized or catatonic behavior； and， negative symptoms (i.e.， diminished emotional expression or avolition)"(APA，2013， p. 99). Moreover， at a minimum， one of the two required T SsyyImptoms of schizophrenia must be delusions， hallucinations， and/or disorganized speech. Changes to the diagnostic criteria for schizophrenia from earlier editions include the removal of： distinct clinical subtypes (i.e.， disorganized， catatonic， paranoid， and undifferentiated) and the special treatment of bizarre delusions. Also， a specifier for catatonic features was added along with dimensional assessment measures in Section III for psychopathology 删除1:<u>(APA， 2013)</u>.

【4】The diagnosis of Schizoaffective Disorder includes the same symptom display as schizophrenia. However， in addition to having these active-phase psychotic symptoms， the client simultaneously has mood symptoms that constitute either a major depressive or manic episode .

【6】While this diagnosis requires the schizophrenic Criterion A and major mood symptoms to co-occur， during the life course of the illness there must be a period of at least 2 weeks when only the schizophrenic symptoms are evident. A life course perspective was emphasized over episodic， and “that the mood symptoms meeting criteria for a major mood episode must be present for the majority of the total duration of the active and residual portion of the illness”(APA， 2013， p. 107). This disorder is usually diagnosed after examination of a rather extensive history of severe symptoms. Since the symptoms can be difficult to distinguish from other schizophrenic spectrum psychosis the use of dimen-sional assessments measures is critical (which can be found in Section ⅡI). Also， catatonia was added as a specifier as well as a distinct disorder 删除1:<u>(APA， 2013)</u>.

【7】A series of diagnoses exists for describing psychotic symptoms that are caused by a general medical condition， health problem， or that are substance induced. To reach an accurate diagnosis， these must first be ruled out as they can lead a person to appear schizophrenic. In Substance-Induced Psychotic Disorder， the induced psychosis (delusions/hallucinations) is due to the effects of a substance/medication. Here， coding is based on the predominant substance with specifiers to denote whether onset during intoxication or withdrawal， and severity is specified. For Psychotic Disorder Associated with Another Medical Condition， hallucinations， delusions， or disorganized speech are the result of another illness and coded based on the predominant symptoms.

【8】Catatonia can occur in many mental disorders and other medical conditions. It is indicated through 12 psychomotor disturbances that are listed in the DSM-5(for examples see DSM-5，p. 119). In Catatonia Associated with Another Mental Disorder， 3 or more of the symptoms of catatonia present during the course of another mental disorder (e.g.， bipolar disorder)， which is coded first along with the catatonia specifier. For Catatonic Disorder due to Another Medical Condi-tion， 3 or more of the symptoms of catatonia present but the cause is believed to be physiological caused by another medical condition 删除1:<u>(APA， 2013)</u>.

【9】To complete this section， the next two categories are used when the criteria for any of the disorders in the schizophrenia chapter are not met. First， Other Specified Schizophrenia Spectrum and Other Psychotic Disorder is used when the symptoms and distress typical of schizophrenia and other psychotic disor-ders present but do not meet the full criteria for any of the Psychotic Disorders defined in this section. It is used to communicate why the client’s symptoms do not meet the criteria， which is included in the diagnosis (for examples see APA，2013， p. 122). The category Unspecified and Other Specified Schizophrenia Spectrum may be used when presenting symptoms and distress/impairment are similar to schizophrenia spectrum disorders but do not meet the full criteria for any other disorder in this spectrum class； and the clinician decides not to communicate the reason， usually due to lack of available information to make a more specific diagnosis 删除1:<u>(APA， 2013)</u>.

【10】**Assessment**

As in the assessment of Delirium and Other Neurocognitive Disorders， the thought disorders common to clients with diagnoses in this section have con-strained the development of self-report instruments. Broad-based approaches，|删除1换行|like the MMPI-2， MMPI-Adolescent (A) and MMPI-2 Restructured Clinical(RC)  offer self-report approaches to diagnosing these disorders. Frequently， however， clients with these disorders do not yield valid results for interpretation with scores showing a tendency of bias in relation to race 删除1:<u>(Monnot， Quirck， Hoerger， & Brewer， 2009)</u>. Generally， assessment of individuals with psychosis is accomplished through structured interviews of both the individual and family in order to establish a psychiatric diagnosis. Generally referred to as Mental Status Examinations， these approaches are designed to accrue information about the quality of the client’s mental pro-cesses. From this general approach， a number of structured or semistructured clinical interviews have been developed  and are used with this population.

【12】In addition， several interview-based clinical rating scales are commonly used with clients diagnosed with schizophrenia or other psychotic disorders. Given the wide range of symptoms in schizophrenia spectrum disorders and the absence of a universal standard for what constitutes an improvement or remis-sion， most of the commonly used scales rely on measuring changes or reduction from baseline scores 删除1:<u>(Leucht， Davis， Engel， Kissling， & Kane， 2009； Liberman，2002)</u>. Nor， as Sawamura， Morishita， and Ishigooka， (2010) point out， is there agreement in terms of which instrument(s) are best for assessing schizophrenia. Further complicating assessment is the fact that more than half of the individu-als with schizophrenia also have a comorbid substance use disorder at a rate that is three times higher than in the general population 删除1:<u>(Green， 2000； Bennett，2009； Regier et al.， 1990)</u> as well as significant concurrent medical illnesses删除1:<u>(Muir-Cochrane， 2006)</u>.

【13】The oldest and still extensively utilized of these approaches is the Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale 删除1:<u>(BPRS； Overall & Gorham， 1962)</u>. This instrument addresses 16 to 24 symptom dimensions that were empirically derived from data from the 1950s. The BPRS has been widely used to monitor clients， particularly in case-management settings. The most commonly used version is the 18-item scale (both observed and reported items) that are rated on a7-point Likert scale from 1“not present"to 7“extremely severe” 删除1:<u>(Mueser， Curran， & McHugo， 1997； Shafer， 2005)</u>. The validity and psychometric strength of the BPRS has been established in a number of studies and factor analysis as an effective measure of psychiatric symptoms 删除1:<u>(Hafkenscheid，1991； Hedlund & Vieweg， 1980； Shafer， 2005)</u>. Overall and Rhodes (1982) reported high sensitivity to change and excellent inter-rater reliability with instruction in the instrument's administration and interview process删除1:<u>(Mortimer， 2007)</u>. However， as in other observer rating scales uniformity in definition is necessary for reliability， for example， what is the meaning for a given scale value such as total score or threshold values； and whether or not any relationship exists between a change in a rating scale symptom and outcome status is still uncertain 删除1:<u>(Leucht et al.， 2005； Mortimer， 2007； Shafer， 2005)</u>. It has been noted that inter-rater reliability can be improved by training in the instrument and often is improved with detailed anchor descrip-tors. Other disadvantages include limited sensitivity to negative symptoms in dual diagnosis patients 删除1:<u>(Burger， Yonker， Calsyn， Morse， & Klinkenberg，2003； Hedlund & Vieweg， 1980； Lykke， Hesse， Austin， & Oestrich， 2008； Mortimer， 2007)</u>.

【15】The Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale 删除1:<u>(PANSS； Kay， Fiszbein， &Opler， 1987)</u> was developed to focus on the distinction between negative and positive symptoms. While the debate continues regarding how best to catego-rize schizophrenic symptoms  the PANSS has become the most commonly used scale with schizophrenia especially in drug trials and clinical research. Its 30 items are rated hased on interviews with the client as well as avail-able clinical records. Clinicians are provided with definitions and anchoring criteria for rating of psychiatric symptoms and functioning on a 7-point scale. Scores for the three scales (positive symptoms， negative symptoms， and general psychopathology) and a total score (range from 30-210) are at-tained by summing items with higher scores indicative of greater pathology. This scale takes approximately 35-45 minutes to administer. The strong psy-chometric properties of the PANSS are well established 删除1:<u>(Linden， Scheel， &Rettig， 2007)</u>. Recent item analysis for the positive and negative subscales showed they were more discriminating than the general psychopathology subscale and more sensitive than the total score 删除1:<u>(Santor， Ascher-Svanum， Lindenmayer， & Obenchain， 2007)</u>. Additionally， using symptom severity scores based on the work of Leucht et al.， (2005)01， Andresen et al.， (2005)established two cutoff scores that signify symptom remission： low symp-tom severity (total score of 60 or less) and moderate/low symptom severity(total score of less than 75). Opler， Yang， Caleo， & Alberti (2007) report the validity of these cutoffs as having good predictive value with high specificity and sensitivity. The advantage of using an instrument like the PANSS is in its simple design that allows for uniformity in terms of the ability to measure an individual's symptoms at various stages over the duration of an illness删除1:<u>(Mortimer，2007)</u>. A shorter 6-item version has been developed with high in-ternal validity to the original 删除1:<u>(Yamamoto，Inada， Shimodera， Morokuma，&Furukawa， 2010)</u>. However， mathematical problems with the scale (interval vs. ratio) are leading to a call for standardized procedures for calculations删除1:<u>(Obermeier et al.，2011)</u>.

【16】The Clinical Global Impression-Schizophrenia 删除1:<u>(CGI-SCH； Haro et al.，2003)</u> is an adaptation of the original Clinical Global Impression scale 删除1:<u>(Guy，1976)</u> for schizophrenia. This brief instrument takes only minutes to complete and assesses just two items： illness severity (from the past week) as well as the degree of change/improvement from baseline/last evaluation based on clinical judgment 删除1:<u>(Haro et al.， 2003)</u>. For each item， five symptom categories (e.g.，pàsi-tive， negative， depressive， cognitive， and overall severity) are rated on a 7-point Likert scale with clearly defined anchors. Illness severity is rated from 1 (nor-mal， not ill) to 7 (among the most severely ill) and Degree of Improvement from1(very much improved) to 7 (very much worse) as well as a “not applicable”category for use when previous information is unavailable. The CGI-SCH has demonstrated good psychometrics with inter-rater reliability in compari-son to PANSS scores. Pearson correlations were high for positive (.86)， nega-tive (.80)， and cognitive (.78) symptoms but lower for depressive symptoms(.64 compared to .80)； sensitivity was found for global assessment except for the depressive dimension 删除1:<u>(Haro et al.，2003)</u>. The CGI-SCH is recommended for both research and clinical practice 删除1:<u>(Haro et al.， 2003； Leucht & Engel，2006； Mortimer， 2007)</u>.

【18】Most people diagnosed with a psychotic disorder are not violent. However， dan-gerous behavior (directed at either oneself or others) may occur in the course of a psychotic episode. For individuals with severe mental illnesses， a plan of action in case of psychiatric emergencies is critical. Clinical assessment of individuals with schizophrenia must include an assessment for violence as well as screening for the presence of suicidal ideation and behavior.Debate surrounds the associa-tion between violence and individuals with serious mental illness. Some studies report an increased risk for violence among persons with serious mental illness删除1:<u>(Douglas， Guy， & Hart， 2009)</u>. Often it is family members and social acquain-tances (excluding self-harm) most at-risk for being targets of this violence 删除1:<u>(Estroff， Swanson， Lachicotte， Swartz， & Bolduc， 1998)</u>. Others find the risk for violence and schizophrenia is minimal unless there is a comorbid substance use disorder删除1:<u>(van Dorn， Volavka， & Johnson， 2012)</u> and that this risk is no greater than the risk for violence in the general population with comorbid substance abuse 删除1:<u>(Fazel， Gulati， Linsell， Geddes， & Grann， 2009；Reichhart & Kissling， 2010)</u>. According to the National Alliance on Mental Illness (NAMI) the majority of violent acts committed by individuals with serious mental disorders are the result of lack of treatment or inappropriate/inadequate treatment of their illness 删除1:<u>(NAMI， 2010)</u>. Frequently it is the untreated 1% of individuals with severe mental illnesses that are most responsible for this violence (e.g.， approximately 10% of all homicides) in the United States 删除1:<u>(Torrey， 2013)</u>. Many studies have shown that treatment reduces violent behavior in individuals with psychiatric disorders and that they are more likely to be a victim of violence than the perpetrator 删除1:<u>(Brekke， Prindle， Bae， & Long， 2001； Dean et al.， 2007； Stuart， 2003； Teasdale， 2009)</u>.

【19】People diagnosed with schizophrenia suffer from extreme prejudice and discrimination and face social stigma 删除1:<u>(Pescosolido， Medina， Martin， & Long，2013； Read， Haslam， Sayce， & Davies， 2006)</u>. Further， when people with psychotic disorders become violent， the behavior is much more frequently aimed at themselves than at others. Internalized stigma often results in hopelessness as well as an increased risk for suicide 删除1:<u>(Pompili. Ruberto. Kotzalidis. Girardi.&saker 2008)</u> As a resmlt neat Tatarelli， 2004； Yanos， Roe， Markus， & Lysaker， 2008). As a result， nearly5% of people diagnosed with schizophrenia are at a high risk for suicide dur-ing their lifetimes， especially near illness onset 删除1:<u>(Palmer， Pankratz， & Bostwich，2005)</u>. Suicide is the leading cause of premature death for people with schizo-phrenia 删除1:<u>(Pompili et al.， 2004； McGrath，Saha， Chant， & Welhan， 2008)</u>. More-over， previous suicide attempts are an important risk factor for suicide among individuals with schizophrenia for both genders and highest in dual diagnosed males 删除1:<u>(Kelly， Shim， Feldman， Yu， & Conley， 2004； McLean， Gladman， &Mowry， 2012)</u>. Suicide risk factors include being young (three times higher than for adults)， being male， history of substance use/abuse， and depression as well as past suicide attempts 删除1:<u>(Pompili et al.， 2007)</u>. Throughout the United States， potential for danger as a result of mental illness is grounds for invol-untary psychiatric hospitalization. Further， people having psychotic benaviors may be substantially less able to care for themselves and/or utilize judgment in their own behalf. Practitioners must peruse the legal statutes in their states to determine whether this type of debilitation constitutes grounds for involuntary hospitalization. In any event， practitioners should familiarize themselves with local resources and procedures for involuntary hospitalization.

【4】**In T. tonsurans and T. violaceum infections， a relatively non-inflammatory type of patchy baldness occurs. Formation of black dots (swollen hair shafts) as the affected hair breaks at the surface of the scalp is a classical sign in this condition， but such findings may not be very conspicuous. The patches， which are usually multiple， may show minimal scaling， sometimes mimicking discoid lupus erythematosus or seborrhoeic dermatitis. They are commonly angular in outline rather than round. A low-grade folliculitis is often seen， and sometimes a frank kerion may develop.**

【5】**Favus**

【6】**Infection with T. schoenleinii is seen sporadically in many countries including South Africa， those of the Middle East， Pakistan， the USA， the UK and Australia. The classical picture of tinea capitis due to this organism is characterized by the presence of yellowish， cup-shaped crusts known as scutula. Each scutulum develops round a hair， which pierces it centrally. Adjacent crusts enlarge to become confluent， forming a mass of yellow crusting. Many patients may show less distinctive changes， in early cases perhaps amounting to no more than perifollicular redness and some matting of the hair. Extensive patchy hair loss with cicatricial alopecia and atrophy among patches of normal hair may be found in long-standing cases where much of the hair loss is irreversible due to the destruction of the bulge area of the hair follicle . In these patients the glabrous skin is commonly affected by the development of similar yellowish crusts. Some nail involvement is found in 2-3% of patients. Although the initial infection probably occurs in childhood in nearly all cases， it shows little if any tendency to clear spontaneously at puberty， particularly in women. Families with severalgenerations affected are well recognized.**

【7】**Differential diagnosis**

【8】The differential diagnosis of tinea capitis includes all conditions capable of causing patchy baldness with inflammatory changes of the scalp. Alopecia areata may show erythema， and although it is itself not a scaly condition， it may coexist with seborrhoeic dermatitis. Such cases can be confusing， though careful examination usually shows that the scaling and the hair loss are not coextensive. Exclamation mark hair must be distinguished from the broken hairs of tinea capitis. Traumatic alopecia from hairdressing procedures and trichotillomania may also be confused. Seborrhoeic dermatitis is usually more diffuse than tinea capitis， but in pityriasis (‘tinea') amiantacea， the changes are often localized. In this condition the scaling is adherent to the hair， but breakage of the hair shaft does not normally occur. In psoriasis， hair loss is found only occasionally and again broken-off hairs are not usually present.

【9】**In impetigo， which may be secondary to pediculosis capitis， loosening of the hair is not normally present， but matting and crusting may cause confusion with inflammatory ringworm. An abscess of the scalp is much more acutely painful， typically causing systemic upset and fever， and shedding of loosened hair is much less evident than in kerion. Discoid lupus erythematosus， lichen planus and other causes of cicatricial alopecia may sometimes have to be considered.**

【10】**Control**

It is of considerable importance with scalp fungal infection to discover the species involved. Some information may be obtained from the clinical picture or the presence or absence of fluorescence， but culture is required for a diagnosis to be accurately established.Where animalspeciesare concerned the source should be proved mycologically： it is not always the expected one. The course of action to be taken|删除1换行|depends upon the situation and the value placed upon the animal. A small， much-loved domestic pet can often be treated successfully and economically with griseofulvin. Cattle ringworm in calves will normally settle spontaneously. A group of highly infected laboratory mice should probably be destroyed.

【12】With anthropophilic infections， careful investigation of the outbreak or epidemic is recommended， and exclusion of children from school is probably necessary. Apart from the risk of spreading infection， there is often a sound sociological basis for keeping an infected child at home. It demonstrates social awareness and responsibility by the family and avoids a situation in which the family may be accused of spreading infection. With zoophilic infections such as M. canis ringworm， children can normally be allowed to remain at school as infectivity from human to human is low.

【13】**Treatment**

【14】The mainstay of treatment in all these conditions is oral griseofulvin， though trials of the newer antifungals have shown very promising results.， Topical therapy has little place， except as an adjunct to oral therapy； it is sensible to remove matted crusts and to carry out routine frequent shampooing. Although massive， single-dose griseofulvin therapy and intermittent dose schedules (25 mg/kg twice a week) have had some success， in general， conventional continuous daily or twice-daily griseofulvin treatment is advisable. In smallspore ectothrix infections， griseofulvin for 4-6 weeks is usually adequate. Where possible， infected hair should be clipped away to reduce the infectivity of the patient and careful monitoring is recommended. In chronic T. tonsurans _T. schoenleinii_ infections， much longer therapy may be needed.

【15】In a study of griseofulvin versus the new oral antifungals， mycological or clinical cure was reported in over 80% treated.'Monotherapy with oral terbinafine， itraconazole and fluconazole all showed similar efficacy in tinea capitis over a 2-3 week period with fewer side effects than a 6 week course of griseofulvin. For M. canis infections a longer course than 3 weeks is advised.

【16】**With scalp kerions， removal of crusts using wet compresses should not be neglected， and the possibility of coexisting bacterial infection should be considered. If confirmed by culture， systemic antibacterial chemotherapy should be instituted. In general， the kerions are less painful than their inflammatory appearance suggests， but analgesics mayv be needed. Occasionally， in children with extensive kerions， admission to hospital or frequent attendance at the out-patient clinic， where skilled nursing is available， may be of great value， and is much appreciated by the worried parents. Permanent hair loss from scarring is usually less than would be expected. Ketoconazole shampoo may be used to prevent spread in the early phases of therapy. In severe inflammatory forms there is a case for using oral prednisolone to inhibit the inflammatory response， and， indeed， a short period of oral corticosteroids also helps by resolving the oedema and oozing and by preventing secondary scarring.**

【50】**CONTACTDERMATITIS**

【51】**Contact dermatitis (contact eczema) maybe conveniently defined， for the present purposes， as an inflammatory condition of the skin caused by an external agent. If photodermatitis is excluded， two broad divisions are recognized： irritant and allergic dermatitis.**

【52】**Irritant dermatitis**

A skin irritant is defined as a substance that is capable of causing cell damage in most people if it is applied for a sufficient length of time， with sufficient frequency and in|删除1换行|sufficient concentrations. The scalp is generally considered to be resistant to irritant damage， possibly because of a relatively thick epidermis and horny layer， and a rapid epidermal ‘turnover time’； i.e. it replaces its natural barrier layer relatively quickly both spontaneously and after any cell damage. It should be noted， however， that substances that are recognized as highly irritant on other sites are rarely applied to the scalp with sufficient frequency for a sufficient time or in sufficient concentrations. For example， hairdressers frequently develop irritant contact dermatitis of the hands from contact with shampoos， but the dilute shampoo solution applied to the scalp does not cause dermatitis because it is soon rinsed off. Shampoos may rarely irritate the skin of the forehead and scalp margins in susceptible individuals， such as those with atopic eczema， and inflame the conjunctival surface of the eye.**

【54】**In practice， thioglycollates， bleaching preparations and heat are the commonest causes of irritant dermatitis of the scalp. It is important to remember that irritant dermatitis affects only skin that has been in direct contact with the offending agent.**

【55】**Allergic dermatitis**

【56】**Allergic dermatitis implies dermatitis due to the development of allergy to a substance previously applied to the skin. Most substances causing dermatitis of this type are of small molecular mass， less than 10 kDa， and act only as partial antigens or haptens. To form complete antigens， they must combine with epidermal protein. The immunological response requires the presence of epidermal Langerhans’cells to recognize the allergen and normal regional lymph glands for the cell-mediated antibody response to occur in the epidermis. The dermatitis developing in this way may spread away from the site of contact， particularly if the allergen is applied repeatedly. The scalp is relatively resistant to allergens. As with irritants， this resistance may be due to the thick horny layer， but this cannot be the only factor， since eczematous contact allergy is not entirely dose related.**

【57】Less well defined is the occurrence of immediate-type hypersensitivity with or without concurrent eczematous allergy. This type I reactivity is most commonly seen with hair dyes of paraphenylenediamine type.

【58】**Clinical appearance**

【59】**Irritant dermatitis affecting the scalp may commence with burning or soreness and tightness of the scalp within a short time of contact with the irritant. Liquid irritants most typically cause these symptoms at the scalp margins. The signs vary from slight erythema to marked oedema and exudation. Complete resolution usually takes no more than a few days. Hair breakage may occur from certain substances， e.g. thioglycollates. If the scalp inflammation is severe enough， diffuse hair loss may occur days to weeks after the insult， due to local inflammatory telogen effluvium.**

【1】The lung interstitium is the area between the gas-exchanging alveolar epithe-lium and the capillary membrane. Normally this space is very thin and allows for effective gas exchange. When diseases or toxins damage the intertitium， it may become infiltrated with inflammatory cells and， ultimately， scar tissue. These interstitial lung diseases produce an impairment in the diffusion of oxygen and lead to respiratory symptomatology. The chest radiograph characteristically shows what is often called a reticular or linear pattern of infiltration.

【2】The term "diffuse parenchymal lung disease" may be more appropriate since these diseases may involve the airways and airspaces in addition to the interstitium. The mnemonic "IS IT IPF?" summarizes the primary causes of inter-stitial disease.

【3】2\. One of the most commonly encountered interstitial lung diseases is idio-pathic pulmonary fibrosis， IPF. Sarcoidosis is also very common and has myriad systemic manifestations. Immunologic/collagen-vascular diseases have well-described systemic features and pulmonary involvement. Lung disease is oc-casionally the initial finding in patients with collagen-vascular diseases. Treatment-related causes must be carefully considered since removal of the of-fending agent is critical. A complete occupational and environmental history is mandatory to exclude inhalational lung disease. Avoidance of the inciting agent is mandatory for the patient， and other persons at risk may be identified. Pulmonary infections， ARDS， and other lung injuries may result in post-inflamma-tory fibrosis and permanent parenchymal changes. Finally， a number of unusual familial diseases have associated interstitial lung disease.

【4】3\. The history and clinical examination sometimes suggest an etiology for inter-stitial disease， such as an exposure or an underlying disease. The chest radio graph may show characteristic patterns which may also suggest an etiology. For example， certain diseases more commonly have predominantly upper lobe in-volvement， including Ankylosing spondylitis， PIE (chronic eosinophilic pneumo-nia)， Intections (TB， histoplasmosis)， Coal worker's pneumoconiosis/silicosis， Eosinophilic granuloma (histiocytosis X}， and Sarcoidosis/berylliosis ("APICES"). A predominantly lower lobe pattern of disease is seen in asbestosis， alveolar pro teinosis， IPF， collagen-vascular diseases， and chronic hypersensitivity pneumonitis. Nodules suggest sarcoidosis， Wegener's， inhalational exposures (pneumoco-nioses)， rheumatoid arthritis， or lymphomatoid granulomatosis "SWIRL"). The pres-ence of pleural disease is unusual in interstitial lung disease， but may be seen in asbestosis， lymphangitic carcinomatosis， and collagen vascular diseases. Normal or increased lung volumes and cystic changes are seen in only a few diseases. Finally， lymphadenopathy is also unusual in interstitial lung disease and may in-dicate sarcoidosis， amyloidosis， lymphangitic carcinomatosis， or berylliosis.

_4\._ Diffuse parenchymal lung disease most often leads to increased lung elastic-ity and a reduction in lung volumes. Pulmonary function tests usually reveal a re-strictive ventilatory defect. Occasionally interstitial disease is seen in a patient|删除1换行|with normal or increased lung volumes， and this narrows the differential con-siderably. The causes of interstitial lung disease with normal or increased lung volumes are summarized by the mnemonic LET'S BRONCH： LAM， Eosinophilic granuloma (histiocytosis X)， Talc injection (intravenous drug abuse)， Sarcoidosis， Bronchiectatic diseases (e.g.， cystic fibrosis)， Respiratory bronchiolitis， Obliter-ative bronchiolitis， Neurofibromatosis， COPD +ILD， Hypersensitivity pneumonitis.(This mnemonic is adapted from one invented by Robert Shpiner， MD.) Exceptions are hypersensitivity pneumonitis and eosinophilic granuloma， which most often show restriction on pulmonary func-tion testing despite normal or increased lung volumes.

【87】1.There are many different types of fluid that may enter the pleural space. Similar to pulmonary infiltrates， pleural fluid may consist of pus， edema， hemor-rhage， immunologic reactions， or tumor cells (PE HIT). These are the major causes of fluid in the pleural space. However， other types also may gain access， such as dialysis fluid， inflammatory fluid from a ruptured esophagus， chyle from injury to the thoracic duct， urine， bile， total parenteral nutrition (TPN)， ascitic fluid， or pancreatic fluid (DECUB TAP). There even have been cases of CSF(pleuro-duro fistula) and stool (fecothorax) in the pleural space. 【88】_2\._ When a pleural effusion is discovered， decubitus films should be obtained to see if the fluid flows freely. Thoracentesis should then be performed without delay on freely flowing fluid. Thoracentesis is indicated in virtually all newly diagnosed， free-flowing pleural effusions. Exceptions to this rule are when the clinical diagnosis is certain (e.g.， CHF) or there is only a small amount of fluid in the pleural space.3. Pleural effusions are broadly categorized as transudates or exudates. Transudates occur when systemic factors that influence the formation and ab sorption of pleural fluid are altered. The most common causes are lelt ventricular failure， pulmonary embolus， and cirrhosis. Others include nephrotic syndrome， peritoneal dialysis， myxedema， atelectasis， and urinothorax. Urinothorax is the only cause of an acidic transudate.

【89】_4\._ Exudates occur when local factors that influence the formation and absorpr tion of pleural fluids are altered. The most common causes are bacterial pneu-monia， malignancy， viral infection， and pulmonary embolus. Pulmonary embolus may cause either a transudate or an exudate depending on whether infarction and hemorrhage occurs. Cancer and hypothyroidism also may cause either a transudate or exudate.

The diagnosis may be elusive： several new di-agnostic studies are available. There is evidence that an elevated adenosine deaminase level may be helpful in establishing a diagnosis of tuberculous pleu-ritis. A second promising diagnostic test is a polymerase chain reaction assay specific for mycobacterial disease. This test may be applied to sputum samples and has been used for analysis of pleural and other body fluids. It has a high degree of sensitivity， with probably a lesser degree of speciticity.

【104】9\. A low glucose is characteristic of rheumatoid arthritis effusions. Other entities that may have a very low glucose include empyema， malignancy， tuberculosis， SLE， and esophageal rupture.

【105】10\. Bloody fluid may be seen in many conditions， but an RBC count greater than 100，000 suggests trauma， malignancy， pulmonary embolism， post car-diac injury syndrome， or asbestos pleuritis (IT BLED-Intravenous catheter， Trauma， BAPE \[benign asbestos pleural effusion\]， Lung cancer， Embolism， Dressler's syndrome).

【106】11\. A pleural fluid amylase level occasionally is helpful. The mnemonic AMY-LASE UP (Adenocarcinoma， Mycobacteria， Yorking (esophageal rupture)， Liver disease， Acute pancreatitis， Serum hyperamylasemia， Ectopic pregnancy， Ureteral obstruction， Pseudocyst) can help you remember related disorders. Hydronephrosis and other disease states that lead to an elevated serum amylase also increase the pleural fluid amylase level. The highest levels are seen in pan-creatic disease， and usually are greater than 20. In other causes including cancer the pleural fluid/serum amylase level is usually about 10. Pancreatic pseudocysts typically have the highest amylase levels， often greater than100，000. Amylase isozyme analysis may be helpful in pinpointing the cause of a high pleural fluid amylase. A high salivary isozyme level indicates malig-nancy， whereas a high pancreatic isozyme level indicates pancreatic disease. The most common malignancies causing a high pleural fluid amylase are lung or ovarian carcinoma. This fact can be helpful in differentiating lung carcinoma from mesothelioma， because mesotheliomas do not make amylase.

【107】12\. A high percentage of eosinophils in the pleural space usually indicates the presence of air or blood. Eosinophils may accumulate after a pneumothorax or hemorrhage into the pleural space. Other causes of pleural fluid eosinophilia in-clude certain drugs such as dantrolene， pulmonary emboli， parasitic infections， fungal infections， and malignancies. Benign asbestos pleural effusion (BAPE) is a complication of asbestos exposure that may occur 10-15 years after the ini-tial exposure. Because the pleural effusion is bloody， a high eosinophil count may be seen with BAPE as well. The mnemonic BAPE (Blood， Air， Parasites， Emboli) summarizes the primary causes of pleural fluid eosinophilia.

【108】13.Suspect the presence of lymphatic fluid in the pleural space (chylothorax} when effusions reaccumulate rapidly or have a milky color. The fluid is not always milky， however， and may be turbid or bloody. Conditions that commonly
lead to the accumulation of lymphatic fluid (chyle} include trauma， malignancy(especially lymphoma)， chest surgery， coughing， vomiting， or straining. A great number of other conditions may be associated with a chylothorax as well， in-cluding LAM； yellow nail syndrome； infections leading to thoracic lymphade nopathy， including tuberculosis and fungal infections； filariasis； aortic and pulmonary aneurysms； and certain congenital syndromes， for example Down’s syndrome， Noonan's syndrome， and Turner's syndrome.

【109】Some major etiologies of chylothorax are summarized by the mnemonic

【110】CHYLES-Cough/strain/vomiting， Hereditary diseases， Yellow nail syndrome， Lymphoma/LAM/lymph node enlargement， Elephantiasis， Surgery/trauma. All of these conditions lead to obstruction of lymphatics and/or injury to the thoracic duct. A pleural fluid triglyceride level > 110 establishes the diagnosis of chylo-thorax. A level at 50-110 is intermediate and may be indicative of chylothorax. When the level is intermediate， the pleural fluid should be submitted for elec-trophoresis to look for the presence of chylomicrons. When a chylothorax is diag-nosed， establish NPO for the patient， and initiate TPN. Do not attempt aggressive chest tube drainage， as this may lead to nutritional depletion. The thoracic duct may then spontaneously heal； if it does not， surgical ligation may be indicated. _14\._ If the cause of a pleural effusion is not determined after thoracentesis， then pleural biopsy is usually the next diagnostic step. If pleural biopsy fails to yield a diagnosis， then consider an open surgical procedure. Bronchoscopy may be helpful if there is another confirmed pulmonary lesion or hemoptysis， but the yield is quite low for an undiagnosed pleural effusion with an otherwise normal x-ray.15. A small number of exudative effusions elude diagnosis even after open pleural biopsy. Experience shows that about tworthirds of these do not recur， and no diagnosis is established. They are presumed to be a result of infection or other inflammatory process that has resoived. The remaining onethird of cases are eventually found to have a specific diagnosis. Malignancy， usually lymphoma， is the most common cause. A few patients eventually are diagnosed with colla-gen vascular diseases or other miscellaneous diagnoses. Interestingly， in the largest published series， none of the patients with undiagnosed exudative pleural effusions who had surgical biopsy were ever found to have tuberculosis.

【31】10.17 Major Aphthous Ulcers or Sutton’s
---------------------------------------

【32】It was formerly called recurrent necrotic mucosa periadenitis or Sutton’s disease. Currently it is considered the most serious manifestation of aphtous stomatitis. The aphthous ulcers have an increased size (0.5 cm), are more painful and last longer than smaller aphthas. The ulcerations are deeper, giving a crater form, taking from 2 to 6 weeks to heal, and can cause scarring. The number of lesions varies and any oral surface area may be affected, but the predilection for the oral mucosa is typical, and the labial mucosa, lingual belly, soft palate and tonsillar crypts the most commonly affected sites. In patients presenting a course without remission, with significant pain and discomfort, health can be compromised because of the difficulty in eating and psychological stress.

【33】Immunosuppressed patients, especially by HIV virus, may show long-term and repeated episodes of major aphthous ulcers. There is no specific treatment for the condition, and the use of steroids, both local and systemic, has been the drug of choice. Other medications have been used in an attempt to solve the disease, such as chemical cauterization acid, topic aminosalicylic-5 acid, vitamins, hydrogen peroxide, chlorhexidine, tetracycline, dapsone, levamisole, and some studies have shown the use of thalidomide, especially for immunosuppressed patients, saving the necessary precautions.

【18】【发病原理】 惊厥的病因很多，产生的部位也各不相同，但共同的发病机制均是由于神经元的晕厥放电引起了大脑或脊髓功能的短暂性障碍。

【19】大脑皮质神经元的正常结构及代谢过程，主要通过细胞膜对钠、钾离子的不同通透性和细胞排钠蓄钾的能力而使细胞膜维持在稳定的极化状态(膜外带正电，膜内带负电，由于内外离子浓度不同而引起)。如有来自其他神经元的兴奋性冲动，通过突触，降低膜电位差，达到一定阈值，即促成神经元放电，膜电位很快即恢复。另一方面，某些散在的神经元的轴突在突触点释放抑制性递质，如y-氨基丁酸(GABA)，则不易接受兴奋冲动；皮质中抑制性神经元库受到兴奋性刺激后，也可反馈性地起抑制作用。这些机制的相互作用，使皮质神经元保持稳定状态。

【20】遗传和皮质局部的结构或功能异常均可使神经元的稳定状态遭受破坏，而出现持续去极化状态，均可自发或在某些诱发因素作用下产生异常放电，引起惊厥发作。病理性异常放电活动如停留在病灶附近，或通过短的皮质间联合纤维传播至附近皮质不再发展则引起部分性惊厥发作。如放电在局部区域的突触环内运转不绝，引致连续部分性惊厥发作。如异常神经元的放电通过输出纤维传播到丘脑和中脑的网状结构，引起意识丧失，再由弥散性丘脑投射系统反馈至大脑各处皮质，兴奋锥体束和网状脊髓束并下行至运动系统及自主神经中枢，产生继发性全身惊厥发作。原发性全身性惊厥发作也起于上脑干及丘脑，然后向上投射至两侧皮质而产生。

【21】近年发现，与惊厥关系密切的神经递质系统有：①乙酰胆碱、谷氨酸、天冬氨酸等可使细胞膜内外的电位差减小，使膜易发生去极化，产生兴奋性突触后电位，使兴奋易于扩散，有促发惊厥的作用，所以被认为是兴奋性递质；②GABA、甘氨酸、去甲肾上腺素、多巴胺、5-HT等可使突触后膜发生超极化，产生

【22】抑制性突触后电位，使膜更加稳定，减少发生惊厥的可能性，所以是抑制性神经递质。其中尤以 GABA与惊厥发作关系最为密切。内源性吗啡样物质也可能是癫痫性惊厥发作的因素。微量元素如锌、铜、锂、锰等也可能在惊厥的发生机制中起一定作用，据认为可能是通过递质的作用所致。

【23】在发作后不久，惊厥灶的巨大传出冲动可以通过反馈而激活抑制机制，包括惊厥灶周围抑制性神经细胞的活动，胶质细胞对兴奋性物质的回收，以及皮质外抑制机构(包括尾状核和小脑，刺激这些部位可以制止惊厥性放电)的参与，产生长时间的细胞膜超极化。这种弥漫性抑制过程可以减少向惊厥灶的传人性冲动，促使发作性放电停止。此外，在发作时脑部释放一些物质，包括内啡肽、腺苷、肌苷、次黄漂呤、缩胆囊肽等，这些内生物质有抑制惊厥的作用。

【24】引起大脑神经元异常放电的因素有：①缺氧血症：大脑皮质氧消耗量大，对缺氧极为敏感，严重缺氧后影响神经元的能源供应，因此可以引起惊厥发作；②酸碱平衡失调：碱中毒、脑皮质局部 pH改变及神经元内水中毒均可产生惊厥；③脑血流量改变：在有脑部循环障碍基础的病人如动脉硬化或无脉症者，轻微的局部灌注压力变化即可导致严重全身惊厥；④其他代谢紊乱：低血糖影响神经元的能源供应，毒物阻止神经元酶代谢，都使其不能维持稳定的膜电位；体液中钙离子浓度降低(膜的通透性增强)，以及甲状腺素和雌激素的增加，也使神经元膜的兴奋性升高；⑤脑结构改变：如肿瘤和脑膜黏连、大脑皮质的局部胶质增生和瘢痕形成。

【25】除癫痫性发作引起的惊厥外，还有非大脑功能障碍性惊厥。例如由甲状旁腺功能减退引起的手足搐搦症，则主要是血钙过低促使神经肌肉的应激性增加，造成临床上的搐搦；狂犬病则为病毒进人中枢神经系统，包括脊髓和脑，产生反射性兴奋，造成临床上的抽搐；马钱子中毒可对脊髓产生高度选择性兴奋作用，增强脊髓的运动反射，产生强直性脊髓性惊厥。

【26】【病因】

【27】(一)颅内疾病

【28】1.颅内感染 各类病毒性、细菌性及真菌性脑炎、脑膜炎、脑脓肿等。

【29】2.脑外伤 产伤(脑挫伤、颅内出血、硬膜撕裂)、急性颅脑外伤、硬膜下或硬膜外血肿、外伤后瘢痕等。

【30】3.寄生虫病 脑内血吸虫病、肺吸虫病、囊虫

【31】病、包虫病等。

【32】4.血管性疾病 脑血管畸形、脑动脉硬化症、高血压脑病、脑梗死、脑出血、蛛网膜下腔出血、脑血管炎等。

【33】5.肿瘤 大脑凸面的少枝胶质瘤、脑膜瘤、星形细胞瘤等。

【34】6.先天性异常及变性疾病 结节性硬化、脑-面三叉神经血管瘤(Sturge-Weber综合征)、脑发育不全、小头畸形、脑积水、弥漫性硬化、Pick 病和Alzheimer 病晚期等。

【35】(二)全身性疾病

【36】1.感染 中毒性肺炎、中毒性菌痢、败血症、百日咳脑病等。

【37】2.缺氧 一氧化碳中毒、窒息、肺水肿、休克、溺水、严重贫血等。

【38】3.心源性脑缺血 Adams-Stokes 综合征、直立性低血压、颈动脉窦过敏等。

【39】4.代谢、营养及内分泌疾病 低血糖(包括胰岛素过量、胰岛细胞瘤及饥饿性低血糖等)、蛋白质及氨基酸代谢异常、低钙血症、低镁血症、维生素B缺乏症(吡哆醇依赖症)、水电解质与酸碱平衡紊乱、尿毒症、肝性脑病、肺性脑病、糖尿病性酸中毒、甲状腺功能亢进症、甲状旁腺功能减退症、遗传性酶缺陷等。

【40】5.外因性中毒 工业毒物(苯、铅、砷、汞等)，、农药类(有机磷、有机氯)等、药物\[贝美格(美解眠)、洛贝林、尼可刹米、樟脑、戊四氯、番木鳖碱、印防己毒素、氨茶碱、颠茄、阿托品、东莨菪碱、异烟肼、氯丙嗪、呋喃类、解磷定、山道年等\]、植物性(白果、马桑子、地瓜子)等。

【41】6.物理性损害 严重的热射病及日射病、触电 _等。_

【42】7.其他 子痫、结缔组织疾病、嗜铬细胞瘤、停药综合征\[如苯巴比妥、甲丙氨酯(眠尔通)\]、破伤风、狂犬病等。

【43】【诊断方法】

【44】(一)病史

【45】病史询问注意下列几方面：发作前有无先兆(如腹部症状、特殊感觉等，先兆常提示大脑皮质局部有病灶)、发作时有无意识丧失、外伤、大小便失禁、发作姿态、面色、声音、肢体抽动顺序、发作时刻(清晨、醒后、睡时、饭后等)、持续时间、对环境的反应及发作后的表现(意识模糊、肢体瘫痪、失语、遗忘、头痛等)。

【46】另外，应针对不同对象，询问发病年龄通用删除1(中):<u>(见表14-1)</u>、发作诱因(发热、饮食过度、外界刺激、过劳、情绪激动等)、发作频率、病程长短、治疗经过、出生和发育史、有关既往史(热惊厥、头部外伤、脑炎、脑膜炎以及寄生虫等病史)、服药史、狗咬伤史、家庭史等。

【49】(二)体格检查

【50】详细的体格检查(包括神经系统检查)对确定惊厥的类别和明确病因都很重要。有意识障碍者多为脑部器质性病变。眼底检查有无视乳头水肿，以了解是否有颅内压增高。发作时瞳孔散大和对光反应消失见于各种原因引起的全身性惊厥发作。局限性神经功能缺失症状如有单瘫、偏瘫、感觉缺失、脑神经麻痹等的发现，有助于病变的定位，且可明确为颅内疾病所引起。Chvostek 及 Trousseau 征阳性均提示低钙惊厥。

【51】(三)实验室和辅助检查

【52】1.脑电图(EEG) 对惊厥性疾病的诊断，特别是对癫痫的诊断、分类、指导药物治疗及判别预后等有重要价值。在癫痫病人的发作间歇期，40%~50%的常规 EEG有阵发异常发现。过度换气、闪光刺激、睡眠或剥夺睡眠等诱发技术能诱发或增强癫痫活动。应用某些特殊电极、多次重复脑电图、长程EEG监测可提高异常波的检测率。长程EEG 录像监测是目前 EEG监测中最先进的一种方法，可同步显示患者的 EEG 与行为变化的关系，可精确确定发作类型，对发作性疾病的诊断最具决定意义。

【53】2.脑脊液 对疑有脑炎、脑膜炎或蛛网膜下腔

【54】出血时可作腰椎穿刺检查脑脊液。

【55】3.其他实验室检查 根据病情，可作血、尿常规、血生化(糖、钙、磷、镁、尿素氮、血脂等)、大便虫卵及肺吸虫皮试等检查。

【56】4.放射学检查 对疑有颅内病变者可选作脑血管造影、CT或MRI 等。

【57】5.其他 正电子发射脑体层扫描(PET)、单光子发射计算机体层扫描(SPECT)等检查，有助于明确仅有脑的功能或代谢改变而无形态学改变的癫痫病灶。

【58】【鉴别诊断】

【59】(一)癫痫发作

【60】癫痫发作分惊厥性和无惊厥性两大类。在呈惊厥的癫痫发作中，有多种发作形式：①全身强直-阵挛性发作(GTCS)：过去称为大发作。部分病人发作初期可有描述不清的“气往上升”、眩晕、幻嗅、幻味或错觉等先兆，持续仅数秒钟。发作时突然出现意识丧失、全身肌肉强直倒地，双眼向上凝视、瞳孔扩大、光反应消失，尖叫、喘鸣或呜咽声，呼吸暂停和青紫，口部先强张而后牙关紧闭，可能咬破舌尖，此时心率增快，血压升高，汗、唾液和支气管分泌增加，并可出现大小便失禁及跌伤。强直期持续10~20s后发生全身性阵挛性抽动，即骨骼肌痉挛和松弛交替出现，并有间断的呼吸声，口鼻常喷出泡沫或血沫，持续2~4min后抽搐停止，呼吸首先恢复，肌肉松弛，进人昏睡，5~10min 后意识逐渐恢复。醒后感到头痛及全身酸痛，不能回忆发作情况。②单纯部分性运动发作：由大脑皮质运动区的痫性放电所引起。以一侧肢体或面部肌肉的阵挛性发作为特征，或自躯体某一部分开始向同侧其他部位扩展(Jackson 发作)，意识一般不丧失，有时放电广泛扩展可引起意识丧失及全身惊厥发作。③肌阵挛性发作：特点是短促的不自主的肌收缩，可侵犯一块肌肉，或一群肌肉，广泛者影响一侧或整个身体，甚至全部肌肉。临床表现为点头、屈臂或突然整个身子屈曲而随之倒地，无明显意识丧失。发作持续1~3s，一日内可多次发作，或每隔数秒钟出现一次，人睡或唤醒时发作更频繁，常伴发于大发作。脑电图显示不规则杂乱的多棘-慢波。④阵挛性发作：全身惊厥发作时主要表现为意识丧失和反复的阵挛性抽动，而无明确的肌强直。此型发作恢复较快。⑤强直性发作：发作时意识丧朱伴全身骨骼肌强烈收缩痉挛，肢体伸直，头、眼常转向一侧，眼睁开或紧闭，常伴有植物神经症状如苍白、潮红、瞳孔扩大等。强直性躯干发作可引起头、颈和躯干伸展，甚至出现角

【61】弓反张。有时此类发作可进展而引起身体转动，某些病人转动可达2~3次。

【62】以惊厥发作为主要表现的癫痫综合征包括：①儿童良性部分性癫痫：是儿童中最常见的癫痫综合征，现分两个：一种是中央-颞区棘波形，多在4~13岁间起病，常有遗传倾向，男性多见，主要表现为一侧面部阵挛性抽搐，极少数偶可进展成 GTCS，多在夜间发作。脑电图在其发作的对侧中央-颞区有高幅棘波。本病预后良好，多在15~16岁前恢复。另一种有光幻觉、黑朦等视觉先兆症状，随后出现半侧阵挛性发作或自动症。部分病人发作后出现偏头痛样头痛。EEG在枕、颞区有阵发性高幅棘-慢波或尖波，称具有枕区放电的儿童良性部分性癫痫。②儿童慢性进行性部分性癫痫状态：又称 Kojewnikow综合征，主要表现为部分运动性发作，晚期常合并肌阵挛发作。EEG 背景活动正常，但有局灶的阵发性棘波和慢波异常。常见病因有运动皮质区的血管性、肿瘤等病变及线粒体脑病。③良性婴儿期肌阵挛性癫痫：见于1~2岁的健康婴儿，常有癫痫或惊厥家族史。表现为全身肌阵挛发作。EEG有阵发性棘-慢波。在青春期可出现 GTCS。④青少年期肌阵挛性癫痫：为遗传性疾病。表现为青春期出现短的不规则、无节律的肌阵挛发作，若累及全身，易导致突然跌倒，意识无障碍。常合并 GTCS。多在觉醒后不久发作。EEG 表现为不规则棘-慢波或多棘-慢波。智力及神经检查正常，治疗效果好。⑤觉醒时 GTCS：多在10~20岁间起病，常有遗传因素。主要或完全出现于清晨醒后或傍晚休息时，可合并有失神发作或肌阵挛发作。⑥婴儿痉挛症(West综合征)：见于一岁以内，最常见于3~6个月时，发作时，颈、躯干、臂的突然屈曲及腿的屈曲和伸展，表现为急剧点头、躯干前屈及两臂向前外侧伸展，意识丧失，可倒地，全部过程仅数秒钟，但常在5~10min内群集发作 15~30次，甚至一日可达100~200次。80%~90%病儿逐渐显示严重的智力发育不全。脑电图上可见杂乱的高幅棘波、多棘波及慢波综合，故又名高幅失律症。⑦Lennox-Gastaut 综合征：也称儿童顽固性癫痫。见于1~8岁小孩，主要发生在学龄前儿童。60%的病孩有患脑病史，多伴有智能发育障碍。发作有多种形式，包括强直性发作、不典型失神发作、无张力发作、肌阵挛发作、GTCS 等。 EEG示背景活动异常，并有阵发性不规则1.5~2.5Hz的棘慢波。发作难以控制，预后不佳。

【63】(二)假性发作

【64】是由心理机制引起的非痫性发作性疾病，又称

【65】心因性发作、癔症性发作等。临床症状复杂而多变，可有精神障碍、运动障碍、感觉障碍及自主神经障碍等，多见于青年女性。全身惊厥性发作为本病最常见的一种表现形式，发作时常突然倒在床上或椅上，双目紧闭，呼之不应，但非真正的意识丧失，肢体阵阵不规则抖动，或单肢不规则抽动，有时呈角弓反张，肢体僵直、屏气或过度换气。一次发作可持续10~20min，或1~2h，可一日发作多次。少数的假性发作患者可出现大、小便失禁、舌咬伤等症状，但无病理征。此类发作持续时间较长，意识及反应均存在，可因暗示而加重或终止，症状常呈戏剧性变化或表演性特征等可与癫痫鉴别，但发作时脑电图检查无特征性痫性放电是与癫痫鉴别的关键。在长期慢性癫痫发作患者中可合并假性发作。

【66】(三)高热惊厥(热性惊厥)

【67】为婴幼儿时期最常见的惊厥原因。一般发生于6个月~5岁的儿童，以1~2岁间最常见。多见于骤起高热至39℃~40℃以上的初期。主要类型为全身阵挛性发作，也有强直性或局限性发作，30%的患儿可有多种发作形式，每次发作数秒至几分钟。高热消退，惊厥即可缓解，惊厥停止后神志即恢复常态，间歇期无神经系体征。2%~3%的患儿以后可能出现癫痫发作。但对发作时间延长或局灶发作、有家族史、首次发作前有神经异常的婴儿发生癫痫的危险较大，为10%~13%。该病不引起精神迟滞、IQ降低、行为障碍等。

【68】(四)手足搐搦症(低钙惊厥)

【69】测镁的血浓度，如血清镁低于0.4~0.6mmol/L则肌注50%硫酸镁0.1~0.2mg/kg 可见速效。

【70】(六)破伤风

【71】因破伤风杆菌侵人皮肤伤口或深组织，其毒素侵袭神经系统的运动细胞而引起局部或全身的痉挛和阵发性抽搐。有2~15d以上的潜伏期，前驱症状为易兴奋、头痛、咀嚼肌无力或酸痛。肌肉痉挛一般先从头部咀嚼肌开始，然后向面部其他肌肉、躯干和四肢等肌肉扩展，最后侵犯膈肌。临床表现为由此引起的牙关紧闭、张口及咽下困难，呈苦笑面容，有排尿困难、角弓反张及呼吸困难等。光、声、轻触等刺激可诱发强烈的阵发性痉挛，病者大汗淋漓、流涎，状甚痛苦，但神志始终清楚，每次数秒至数分钟，抽搐发作间歇期其肌肉仍呈紧张强硬。

【72】(七)狂犬病

【73】又名恐水病，是被狂犬咬伤后，狂犬病毒进人体内后经脊神经背根，也可能通过血流进人中枢神经系统。潜伏期2周~3个月或更长，发病后有数小时至2d前驱期，表现为微热、头痛、食欲不振、兴奋、恐惧不安，对声、光、风等刺激敏感而发生喉部紧缩感。在激动期时，病人高度兴奋、躁动、恐怖、高热，上述各种刺激均易激发痉挛，恐水现象突出，饮水时因咽喉肌痉挛而无法咽下，甚至看到水或听到水声也出现此现象。最后进人麻痹期，病人趋安静，肌肉痉挛停止而表现弛缓性瘫痪。发作期神志始终清楚。严重者可因呼吸及心力衰竭而迅速死亡。

【74】(八)子痫

【75】子痫是重度妊娠中毒症，发生在妊娠24周以后。发作时先有意识模糊，面部及颈项肌肉强直，头扭向一侧，眼球固定，瞳孔散大，口角和面部的肌肉颤搐或抽动，继之全身肌肉强直收缩，历时1~2min后抽搐渐停，转人昏睡状态。尿检可与妊娠性癫痫和癫痫大发作鉴别。子痫病者往往伴有高血压、水肿和蛋白尿，有头痛、头晕、眼花、呕吐等先兆子痫病史可资区别。

【76】(九)过度换气综合征

【77】焦虑状态和其他神经症(神经官能症)患者，可能因主动的过度换气而产生口角和肢端的麻木或感觉异常，可伴有头昏和手足搐搦。诊断时可嘱患者进行过度换气试验，以观察是否能诱发同样的症状。

【78】屏气发作常见于婴幼儿，发生于受挫或愤怒而大哭时，出现呼吸暂停伴紫绀，20~30s 后意识丧失，可有角弓反张，甚至全身阵挛性抽搐，也可有尿失禁。诊断时根据有明显促发因素，绝无夜间出现，呼吸暂停或紫绀出现于意识障碍之前。

【79】(十)维生素B，缺乏和依赖症

【80】维生素B，能影响脑内y-氨基丁酸(GABA)的合成，当 GABA 合成减少时，中枢神经系统会过度兴奋而致惊厥。婴儿缺乏维生素B，可致全身惊厥，维生素B，治疗有效。但如大剂量服用时间过长，则产生对维生素B，的依赖，一旦停药也会引起全身惊厥。母亲妊娠时用大量维生素B，当婴儿出生后，也可发生维生素B，依赖。

【81】(十一)惊厥性晕厥

【82】凡严重的脑缺血或缺氧性晕厥均可能伴有惊厥、昏迷、瞳孔散大、分泌增加，偶伴大、小便失禁，类似癫痫发作。但惊厥的时间较短，一般仅数秒钟，最多数十秒钟。惊厥的形态主要表现为角弓反张，伴有零星的阵挛性痉挛、多在上肢和面部。发作时EEG检查，在深度晕厥时出现8活动，惊厥时呈现电位低平，不发作时无特殊异常。

【83】颈动脉窦征群，一般仅出现血管运动性晕厥，但在有脑部循环障碍的病人，如伴发有动脉硬化或无脉症者，轻微的局部压力可能导致严重的昏迷和全身性惊厥，个别病人还可见对侧的局限性痫性发作或偏瘫。

【84】(十二)中毒性惊厥

【85】某些化学物品，主要是药物，能直接增高神经元的兴奋性，使用过量时易产生惊厥。常见药物有戊四氯、贝美格(美解眠)、野靛碱、二甲弗林(回苏灵)樟脑、茶碱、咖啡碱、肾上腺素、印防己素、哌哔嗪、乌头素、藜芦素、桉叶油、侧柏油、马钱子等；四乙基铅、砷、铊、锡、汞、钛等重金属急性中毒；硫化氢、二硫化碳、戊硼烷、癸硼烷、溴化烷、氰化物、三氯乙烯、苯、硝基苯、甲醇等中毒均可见惊厥。马桑子、蕈中毒等多有惊厥症状，常伴腹痛、腹泻、呕吐等症状。重度一氧化碳中毒，有机氯中毒、蛇毒中毒等均可引起惊厥，多属危重状态。

【86】(十三)代谢性惊厥

【87】很多代谢性疾病均可出现惊厥症状，以尿毒症、低血糖最常见。尿毒症性惊厥发作时和血尿素氮量并无绝对关系，低钠、低钙、高钾和水中毒都可能引起惊厥。病人常见有情绪不稳和性格改变，渐有散发的肌阵挛或震颤，痫性大发作或部分性发作，然后渐渐陷人昏睡或昏迷状态。肾病病史和血、尿化验可提供诊断。

【88】低血糖性惊厥可发生于严重血糖降低如胰岛细胞瘤或胰岛素用药过量时。当血糖低至2.8~3.3mmol/L(50~60mg%)时即可发生惊厥。发作前

【89】第5节 昏 迷

【90】脑功能深度抑制后出现意识丧失和随意运动消失、出现异常病理反射或对刺激无反应时称为昏迷。

【91】【发病原理】人对外界环境和自身做出认识并适当做出反应我们称之为意识。与意识有关的投射系统有两大类，即特异性和非特异性上行投射系统。特异性上行投射系统是各种感觉传入通路的总称，具体说就是各类感觉器官接受机体感觉冲动，经传导束始于丘脑的特异性核团，再传人大脑皮层感觉区，引起大脑皮层觉醒。冲动进入脑干后发出无数侧支到脑干的网状结构，广泛作用于大脑皮层，这个系统称上行网状激活系统(ARAS)。来自内脏的刺激(包括体液的刺激)则进人丘脑下部，称为丘脑下部激活系统，这个系统激活大脑边缘系统。上述两个系统互相联系，大脑觉醒状态就是靠这两个系统维持的，当这两个系统受到损害时，轻者意识障碍，重者昏迷。

【92】【诊断方法】 详细询问病史往往是正确诊断很重要的一个环节。注意昏迷发生原因，了解过去病史，了解有无外伤，服药情况等。进行体格检查，生命指征情况如何，皮肤黏膜有无异常情况。神经系统的检查在意失识障碍的病人显得尤为重要，如意识障碍程度、瞳孔大小、眼底情况、运动，反射情况、有无病理反射等。在上述任务完成之后，有针对性地进行一些辅助检查，以便进一步明确诊断。

【93】【病因】 不外乎两大原因，即颅内疾病或颅外疾病。颅外原因主要是指各种缺血、缺氧性疾病；各种代谢异常引起的代谢性脑病；各种化学物质、药物中毒、食物中毒所致脑损害均可以引起意识丧失或意识障碍。颅内原因主要是指脑的感染，脑的肿瘤，脑的出血性疾病等。

【94】【鉴别诊断】 目的有三，首先是了解昏迷程度，即确定是不是昏迷；其次病因诊断，了解有否糖尿病、肝病、尿毒症，上述疾病在昏迷原因中占有一定比例。肺性脑病、感染性脑病、黏液性水肿、水电解质紊乱、脑肿瘤也是引起昏迷常见原因，应该认真加以鉴别；颅脑外伤，药物中毒等也可以导致昏迷；最后是推测昏迷发生的具体病变部位。根据呼吸、瞳孔、眼球反射性运动，颅内压增高情况等来进一步定位，从而得出病变的准确部位。

【95】第6节 睡眠障碍

【96】睡眠是个复杂的节律性的生理现象。正常人的睡眠是与觉醒交替进行的，每24小时有一觉醒睡眠周期。在觉醒时，机体主动地与外界环境密切联系，并以适当的行动来回答环境的各种变化。在睡眠时，感觉减退，意识逐渐消失，机体与环境的主动联系大大减弱，失去了对环境变化精确适应的能力。临床上，常见的睡眠障碍有如下几种。

【97】一、失眠

【98】失眠为最常见的主诉之一，以人睡困难时常觉醒和/或晨醒过早为主要表现。

【99】【病因】

【100】(一)躯体原因

【101】各种疼痛如牙痛、头痛、搔痒，消化系统疾患如腹泻、恶心、呕吐；呼吸系统疾患如鼻塞、呼吸困难、咳嗽等，循环系统疾患如心悸、阵发性心动过速、高血压等。此外，和睡眠相关的疾病如睡眠呼吸暂停综合症、睡眠周期性动作等都可导致失眠。

【102】(二)环境原因

【103】初到某地、进出夜班、乘坐车船、气温及温度的变化、噪音、光线、气味的变化等也都影响睡眠。

【104】(三)精神原因

【105】兴奋和焦虑最易造成短期的失眠；长期失眠多见于神经衰弱和抑郁症。此外，精神紧张、不安、害怕、恐惧也常导致失眠。

【106】(四)其他原因

【107】许多药物如苯丙胺、咖啡碱、麻黄素、氨茶碱、异丙基肾上腺素均能引起失眠，饮酒、缺氧、中毒、脑外伤、脑血管病、脑肿瘤也可导致失眠。

【108】【发病原理】 对于睡眠的本质仍不十分了解。近年来实验研究证明，睡眠的发生机制是与脑内的网状激活系统以及其他脑内区域的神经控制有关，同时也与脑内神经递质的动态变化有密切关系。从神经机制来说，导致非快眼动睡眠的中枢位于脑干中线的一些神经细胞集中的中缝核，而与快眼动睡眠有直接关系的部位是脑桥背部的蓝斑。参与睡眠的神经递质有多种，如去甲肾上腺素，5-羟色胺，多巴胺，乙酰胆碱等。在去甲肾上腺素含量不变或增高的情况下降低5-羟色胺的含量即可产生失眠，反之引起多眠。有关睡眠因子如慢波睡眠肽睡眠因子等正在研究中。

【109】【诊断方法】

【110】2.生理性警觉水平常提高，呼吸心率较增快，血压轻度增高等。

【111】3.病人易激怒、记忆力、思考力、计算力下降、反应迟钝、严重时可产生幻觉与错觉。

【112】4.睡眠脑电图显示快波睡眠(REM)期缩短，而非快波睡眠(NREM)的第2期较长，第4期提前结束。

【113】二、梦游

【114】梦游是一种睡眠中的自主动作，常见于儿童，多与遗尿并发，发病率1~6%。

【115】【病因与发病原理】 本症的原因尚不十分清楚，通过脑电图观察：在梦游症发作之初出现高波幅的慢波，以后转为低波幅，此种变化相当于睡眠的浅睡阶段。正常人在睡眠时，如果脑的活动水平急剧增高则可引起觉醒，而梦游患者由于觉醒机制障碍，此时脑的活动水平呈不完全觉醒状态，类似于一过性意识混浊状态。梦游症大多数属于功能性变化，但也有器质性病变造成的病例，经观察证明多数病人可在数年后自愈，故推测本症与中枢神经系统发育不健全有关。

【116】【诊断方法】

【117】1.男性儿童多见。部分病人有家族史。

【118】2.反复多次在熟睡中突然坐起或起床，在意识朦胧状态下进行某项活动，如东抚西摸，徘徊走动，目光呆滞，动作笨拙，呼唤不易醒，每次发作持续数分钟至半小时，事后并无记忆。

【119】3.脑电图显示在梦游开始时出现高波幅成群的慢波，持续10~30秒；以后转为慢波节律，发作过后呈现低波幅的快波。

【120】三、夜惊

【121】表现为睡眠中的发作性骚动、叫喊、常伴有心跳、呼吸加快、流汗等植物神经症状。

【122】【病因及发病原理】 此症病因未明，经研究证明夜惊发生于 NREM 睡眠的第4期，入睡后15~30分钟内出现，属于第3、4期突然呈现的“觉醒反应障碍"，脑电图显示觉醒的a节律。

【123】【诊断方法】

【124】1.多见于儿童。

【125】2.睡眠中突然坐起，惊叫、辗转不安或其他复杂的无目的动作，持续1~2分钟，醒后不能记忆。

【126】3.发作时常伴有心率、呼吸增快、多汗等植物神经症状。

【127】4.脑电图突然呈现觉醒状态。

【128】5.排除其他躯体疾病。

【129】四、遗尿

【130】指5岁以上的儿童在日间或夜间反复出现不自主排尿。

【131】【病因】 遗尿症的病因尚未明确，可能与遗传因素、器质性因素或精神因素有关。有人调查发现父母双方之一在幼年患有遗尿者，其子女遗尿的患病率达40%，也有人认为遗尿与泌尿系统解剖或功能异常有关，如膀胱颈发育异常、膀胱容量减少或夜排尿节律改变等。睡眠实验研究发现遗尿多发生于睡眠的第3期或第4期，这时期不易唤醒、而且醒后对遗尿全遗忘。多数学者认为遗尿可能是由于中枢神经成熟延迟，养育方式不当，缺乏卫生习惯的训练或精神因素而产生神经功能失调所致。

【132】【诊断方法】

【133】1.年龄5岁或5岁以上的儿童，白天或晚上经常不自主排尿。

【134】2.遗尿严重程度5~6岁儿童，每月至少有二次遗尿；6岁以上儿童每月至少有一次遗尿。

【135】3.除外神经系统损害、癫痫、躯体疾病或药源性(如精神药物)所致的遗尿。

【136】【鉴别诊断】 尿失禁 尿失禁也指不自主排尿，但无时间性，任何时候均可发生，绝大多数是由于神经系统器质性病变造成的，而遗尿仅发生于睡眠中。

【137】五、发作性睡病

【138】发作性睡病(narcolepsy)是一种原因不明的睡眠障碍，主要表现为长期的警醒程度减退和不可抗拒的，反复发作的睡眠。

【139】【病因】本病病因不明，下丘脑后部病变或大脑脚受损时，可发生发作性脑病和猝倒症，据此推测可能与该部位受损有关，病毒感染、占位性病变压迫、Wornicke 脑病、非洲锥虫病等可能为其病因，更多则认为与遗传有关。近年有人认为本症中可能存在睡眠递质功能的失常。

【140】【发病原理】 本病发病机制未明。由于近年来发现与本症有关的猝倒症，睡眠麻痹和人睡幻觉均匀发生于眼快动睡眠期，且本病患者夜间睡眠浅，易醒，故本病可能与眼快动睡眠期有关。此与正常睡眠和其他过度的睡眠障碍类型不同，发作性睡病表示在白天经过短暂的困倦阶段而突然发生于眼快动睡眠；猝倒症表示眼快动睡眠时的完全肌张力下降；睡眠麻痹则是眼快动睡眠后肌张力下降的继续；人睡幻觉表示正常眼快动睡眠时患有从生动的梦境醒后的继续。

【141】控制睡眠和觉醒有3个系统，即醒觉系统，非眼快动系统和眼快动系统，前两者对眼快动系统有抑制作用，在夜间眼快动睡眠期反复出现是由于眼快动系统的发生超过了非眼快动系统的抑制。发作性睡病是由于醒觉系统对眼快动系统的抑制减弱，因此，在醒觉时可发生眼快动睡眠。

【142】【诊断方法】

【143】1.各年龄均可发病，青年人多见，约10%有家族史。

【144】2.嗜睡发作 是一种白天发作性不可抗拒的睡眠，可发生在任何场合，如骑车、说话、进食时突然人睡。持续数秒钟到数小时，醒后感到暂时清醒，一日可多达数次。

【145】3.猝倒 猝倒发作表现为肌张力突然松驰，使病人跌倒在地，无意识障碍，并能立即站起，大笑、痛哭、发怒时可以诱发。面一般持续约1~2分钟，意识始终清醒。

【146】4.睡眠麻痹 多见于青年人，发生在睡眠与觉醒期间，患者醒后发现自己不能动，只要有人推一下或与其讲话则即刻恢复，时间不超过一分钟。正常人偶尔亦有发生，但发作性睡病患者发作频繁，有时每周数次。

【147】5.人睡幻觉 患者在人睡时出现生动的听或视幻觉和触痛等体觉，内容大多鲜明，常属日常经历，约30%患者有之，也常和睡眠麻痹并见。

【148】【鉴别诊断】 原发性睡眠增多症，常发病于青年男性，表现为睡眠时间过长，可持续数小时到数天，与发作性睡病相比，不是不能克制睡眠。其另一特征是很难从晚间的睡眠中完全转醒，有觉醒后或催眠后的错乱状态，可见于中枢神经系统病变，如脑外伤、脑肿瘤或脑血管病等。

【149】第7节 言语障碍

【150】言语是人类大脑特有的功能，是交流思想的重要工具。言语障碍可分为失语和发音困难，一个意识清晰、精神正常、发育和构音器官无障碍的人，由于主侧大脑半球言语功能区者损伤其说话、听话、阅读和书写能力残缺或丧失称为失语。发音困难可由于发音肌肉瘫痪，共济失调或肌张力变化引起。

【151】一、失语

【152】【病因】 失语症的病因可按其起病的急慢及能否恢复而分为急性起病，缓慢起病及短暂性三类。急性起病中以急性脑血管病最为常见。其中以脑梗死尤为常见，其次为颅脑损伤及急性脑炎。缓慢起

【153】病的失语有脑瘤、颞叶脓肿、硬脑膜下血肿、脑部肉芽肿，其他还有老年前期痴呆及老年期痴呆等，对有性病史的病人出现失语应想到神经梅毒的可能。短暂性脑缺血发作所致的失语起病甚急，一般持续数分钟到数小时，在24小时内能完全恢复。其他造成短暂性失语的病因还有癫痫，偏头痛等。

【154】【发病原理】 发病原理尚未完全明了。传统认为语言是大脑皮质的功能，左侧大脑是人的语言(优势或主侧)半球，左半球内存在与语言有关的仪表区(语言中枢)，言语运动中枢位于左侧额下回后端的盖部及三角部皮质(Broca)；感觉性(感度性)语言中枢位于左侧颞上回后部；视运动性语言中枢(书写中枢)在左侧额中后部；视(感觉)性语言中枢(阅读中枢)在左顶下小叶的角回；命名性语言中枢在左侧颞中及颞下回后部(37区)。各个言语仪表区或它们间的神经连结受损后即可产生特异的失语综合症。上述结论多数是根据卒中等脑局限性损害病人的失语表现结合病人死后病理解剖发现的结果。

【155】通过更细致、更广泛的语言学及解剖和病理解剖研究，手术时电刺激脑的地形图、语言作业时测定脑电图，局部脑血流等新技术的引进，特别是本世纪70年代 CT和MRI相继问世后对语言功能的神经机制有了更新更多的认识。

【156】人类各种语言的表达功能确实都定位于语言半球。对语言的理解通常也依赖语言半球，但有相当一部分人对侧半球也具有一定的语言理解功能，语言功能的半球侧化与右、左利手相关。90%~99%的右侧利手者左侧大脑为其语言半球。左利手中50%~70%的语言半球在左侧，余下中的一半明确在右侧，另一半人的左右半球同样地参与语言活动，研究还发现，大脑皮质不能垄断语言功能，语言半球的丘脑也参与语言活动。另有研究发现 Broca 失语病人总有豆状核的损害，手术时电刺激脑的地形图的研究发现，语言皮质的解剖定位和分布在个体间存在相当大的差异，与性别、言语能力等因素有关。皮质语言区由若干个约1cm²大小板块镶嵌构成，不同的镶嵌参与不同的语言功能。同一病人用两种不同语言对同一物体的命名即涉及语言区内不同的镶嵌，与语言表达有关的区域远超出传统的 Broca区，延伸至外侧裂上、下的下顶叶和上颞叶。与口面顺序动作以及言语声编码有关的神经机制也都定位于这个区内。另一方面，CT和病理研究发现，单是Broca 区损害只出现言语失用而不发生 Broca 失语； Broca 失语可无 Broca 区损害，但大多有左侧额-顶岛盖广泛的皮质-皮质下损害，有的涉及颞叶。因

【157】此，各种失语综合症与脑定位损害间并不存在严格的对应关系。

【158】【诊断方法】

【159】(一)运动性失语

【160】病人不能说话或只能讲一两个简单的字且不流利，用词不当，但对别人的言语能理解，对自己用错词也知道，对书写的东西也能理解，但读出来有困难和差错。多数伴右侧偏瘫，以面一臂瘫为更严重，病人正常左手常有意念运动性失用。

【161】(二)感受性失语

【162】病人不能理解别人的言语，自己发音虽然流利，但内容不正常，因为他也不能理解自己的语言，在发音用词方面有错误，严重时不知所云，别人完全听不懂他讲的话，摹仿医生讲话的能力减退，能够书写，写出来的内容有错误、遗漏，抄写能力则相对不受影响。病人虽有言语缺陷，但无内省力，言语增多及欣快。

【163】(三)命名性失语

【164】病人称呼物件或人名的能力丧失，但能叙述某物是如何使用的，别人告知该物的名称时，他能辨别对方讲的对或不对。

【165】(四)失写

【166】病人无手部肌肉瘫痪，但不能书写或写出的句子有遗漏差错，抄写能力则保存。

【167】(五)失读

【168】病人尽管并不失明，但对视觉性符号的认识能力丧失，因此不识词句、图画。病人不能阅读、自发地书写，也不能抄写，常与失写同时存在。

【169】通过与病人的交谈，基本上可以了解患者言语是否流利，有无言语困难及用词不当等文法上的错误，也可通过提问的方式，测验患者对言语的理解力，或从病人重复检查者的言语，以观察病人对听语的接受，口语的表达以及两者之间的联系是否完整。可以选用常用的物品。如火柴、钢笔等测验病人的命名能力。可以通过阅读报纸、诵读单词、短句或从病人写出自己的名字、工作单位等来检查病人的阅读和书写能力。

【170】【鉴别诊断】

【171】(一)失用

【172】丧失了准确执行有目的动作的能力，不能按医生要求去执行各种动作，如伸舌、戈火柴等日常动作，但病人能自发的做这些动作。检查时可通过对病人自发动作的观察，让病人执行简单的动作，摹仿检查者的动作或拼搭积木等，来观察其执行有目的动作的能力。

【173】(二)失认

【174】病人表现对复杂感觉的认识能力丧失，如视觉性失认，即病人能看见物品图画，但不能说出其名称、颜色和作用，见于双侧后枕叶病变。

【175】二、发音困难

【176】【病因】

【177】(一)肌肉疾病 如肌营养不良、重症肌无力、肌炎等。

【178】(二)下运动神经元病变 如面瘫、舌瘫、舌咽和迷走神经麻痹，延髓型灰质炎、重症复发性神经炎、后颅窝肿瘤等。

【179】(三)上运动神经元病变 如假性球麻痹和多发性硬化等。

【180】(四)锥体外系疾病 如帕金森氏病、肝豆状核变性、舞蹈病、遗传性共济失调等。

【181】【发病原理】 由于言语产生的第三阶段-言语表达阶段所包括的各结构的损害，或生理过程的失调，造成脑内言语变成声音，组成言语的运动(构音运动)障碍，从而口语的声音形成困难，严重者则完全不能发音，即造成发音困难。

【182】【诊断方法】

【183】(一)上运动神经元损害造成的发音困难

【184】有造成上运动神经元损伤的疾病，如脑血管疾病、肌萎缩性侧索硬化、脑瘤等病史。查体发现此类发音困难的特点是：构音肌瘫痪、舌较正常为小而硬，言语含混不清，特别是唇音(拨、泼、模、佛等音)及齿音(如知、吃、滋等音)受到严重牵累，此外常伴有吞咽困难、饮水返呛及情感障碍及双侧偏瘫等。

【185】(二)下运动神经元损害造成的发音困难

【186】有造成发音肌本身的疾病，或支配发音肌的下运动神经元损害的疾病历史。检查时可发现舌、软腭、咽部及声带等麻痹的表现，辅助检查可显示异常，如 Guillain-Barro's syndrome 病人脑脊液可出现蛋白细胞分离现象，后颅窝肿瘤病人MRI 或脑室造影常有异常等。

【187】病人有重症肌无力，肌营养不良等肌病史，检查可见有肌肉压痛萎缩等，一般无感觉障碍，血清酶学检查有的可显示异常，重症肌无力病人 Tonsilon 药

【188】物试验阳性可协助诊断。

【189】第8节 瘫 痪

【190】瘫痪是指随意运动肌力的减退或丧失，前者称为轻瘫或不全瘫痪，后者称为全瘫。

【191】【发病原理】 随意运动的完成，除了上、下运动神经元外，还需要正常的肌肉和神经肌肉传导。因此，瘫痪的发病原理及病因可分为上、下运动神经元性、神经肌内传导障碍和肌肉病变引起的三种。

【192】(一)下运动神经元瘫痪

【193】当下运动神经元及其纤维病变时，由于牵张反射等的脊髓反射弧中断，腱反射及肌张力就减弱或消失。肌肉的新陈代谢与支配它的下运动神经元密切有关，故下运动神经元破坏时，引起相应肌肉的新陈代谢障碍而导致肌肉萎缩，可在3个月内减小至肌肉原来大小的20~30%，称为失神经性萎缩。当下运动神经元受损害时(如进行性脊肌萎缩症)，其应激性增高而对其支配的肌纤维有自发性的冲动发放，表现为一个或一个以上运动单位的孤立收缩，称为肌束颤动，可肉眼见到，在肌电图上为大的双相或多相的动作电位，失神经性肌纤维虽不再能对神经冲动起反应，但变为敏感而有个别肌纤维的自发收缩，称为肌纤维颤动，由于非常细小而不能被肉眼见到，只能靠肌电图上识别，为重复的短时程的棘波电位。

【194】下运动神经元损害不久，神经和肌肉的电兴奋即发生数量上和质量上的变化，表现为不完全或完全性的变性反应。

【195】(二)上运动神经元瘫痪

【196】在锥体束急性损害时，瘫痪肢体开始时可表现为肌张力减低，腱反射消失，病理征阴性(此时期称为休克期)；而数天以后出现肌张力增高，腱反射亢进及病理征阳性，这些现象的发生系由于正常大脑皮质运动区及其锥体束和其他核上性纤维对前角细胞(特别是丫运动神经元)经常有一种抑制作用，当大脑皮质运动区或锥体束损害时，这种抑制作用减少或消失，y运动神经元的兴奋性增高所致。

【197】(三)神经肌肉传导障碍及肌肉疾病所致瘫痪

【198】神经肌肉接头处的乙酰胆碱形成减少或分泌障碍，或其受体减少，胆碱酯酶受抑制或运动终板的损害，以及肌细胞内外离子分布的异常，都可引起瘫痪。

【199】【病因】】瘫痪是锥体束、前角细胞、前根、周围运动神经，神经肌肉接头、肌肉等各个部位损害的共

【200】同表现，各种病因均可引起。为了叙述方便，将在诊断和鉴别诊断中探讨有关的病因。

【201】【诊断方法】

【202】(一)下运动神经元性瘫痪

【203】瘫痪的分布以小组肌肉或单个肌肉为主；瘫肌常有萎缩、肌纤维颤动及束颤且肌张力降低，腱反射减退，甚或消失；可有感觉与植物神经功能障碍；没有病理反射；实验室检查，肌电图示失神经电位，肌活检示去神经性变。

【204】(二)上运动神经元性瘫痪

【205】瘫痪的分布以整个肢体或肌群为主；瘫肌张力增高腱反射活跃或亢进，无或轻度废用性肌萎缩；浅反射减退，病理反射阳性；实验室检查，肌电图无肯定阳性肌电图征象。肌活检可示废用性肌萎缩。

【206】(三)神经肌肉传导障碍及肌肉疾病所致的瘫痪

【207】神经肌肉传导障碍导致的瘫，一般都是暂时性的，其瘫痪程度可时有变化，象下运动神经元瘫痪一样可有肌张力下降及腱反射消失，但一般无肌肉萎缩及肌束颤动，也无感觉障碍及病理反射。肌肉疾病所致的瘫痪，有肌肉萎缩，肌萎缩重于瘫痪，可有肌张力和腱反射减低，肌肉可有压痛。实验室检查肌源性瘫痪血肌酶多有升高，肌电图呈肌病性改变，肌活检呈肌病性变。重症肌无力时血清中抗乙酰胆碱受体抗体增加。

【208】【诊断及鉴别诊断】 瘫痪确定以后，可根据瘫痪分布的部位和范围及瘫痪的其他特点，考虑下一步诊断，常见的瘫痪有以下几种。

【209】(一)单瘫

【210】系指一个上肢、下肢或面部的瘫痪。瘫痪呈节段性分布者属前角或前根的损害，单纯前角损害无感觉障碍。前根损害的原因大多继发于脊髓被膜或脊椎骨质的病变，因此后根亦常同时受损，常伴有根性疼痛和节段性感觉障碍。脊膜及脊椎的肿瘤炎症、结核外伤是神经根损害的常见原因。

【211】整个上肢或下肢瘫痪而且伴有感觉障碍时以神经丛损害的可能性大。臂丛损害时整个上肢呈下运动神经元性瘫痪，肩部以下的各种感觉缺失，可由臂丛神经炎、外伤、肿瘤压迫等引起。腰骶丛损害较少见，表现为整个下肢瘫痪和感觉缺失，可由于脊柱结核或脱位、穿通伤、腰大肌脓肿、盆腔肿瘤的压迫等引起。

【14】**GALLBLADDER AND DUCT DISEASES**

【15】**Cholelithiasis**

【16】Gallstones are stone-like masses called calculi (singular： cal-culus) that form in the gallbladder as a result of an imbalance in the composition of bile. There are two types of gallstones：pigment and cholesterol. More than 80% of gallstones in the United States are cholesterol stones.40

【17】Cholelithiasis， the presence or formation of gallstones， can be asymptomatic， detected incidentally during medical imag-ing. Problems arise if a stone leaves the gallbladder and causes obstruction somewhere else in the biliary system， presenting as biliary colic， cholecystitis， or cholangitisS.

【18】It has been reported that cholelithiasis affects 10% to 15%of the adult population， and is the leading cause for hospital-ization secondary to GI problems. Direct and indirect costs related to gallbladder disease have been estimated at $6.2 bil-lion annually in the United States.41 See Box 9.4 for risk fac-tors to watch for in a client’s history that correlate with the incidence of gallstones. Sanslores.

【19】Clients with gallstones may be asymptomatic or may have symptoms of a gallbladder attack described in the next sec-tion. The prognosis is usually good with medical treatment， depending on the severity of disease， presence of infection， and response to antibiotics.

【20】**Biliary Colic**

【21】With biliary colic， the stone gets lodged in the neck of the gallbladder (cystic duct). Pain results as the gallbladder contracts and tries to push the stone through. The classic symptom of this problem is right upper abdominal pain that comes and goes in waves. The pain builds to a peak and then fades away.

Obstructions of the gallbladder can result in biliary sta-sis， delayed gallbladder emptying， and subsequent mixed stone formation. Stasis and delayed gall bladder emptying can occur with any pathologic condition of the liver， hormonal influence， and pregnancy (usually third trimester when the|删除1换行|developing fetus compresses the mother’s gallbladder up against the liver).42

【23】**Cholecystitis**

【24】Cholecystitis， the blockage or impaction of gallstones in the cystic duct ， leads to infection or inflammation of the gallbladder. This condition may be acute or chronic， causing painful distention of the gallbladder. The affected individual may feel a steady， severe pain that rapidly increases in intensity， lasting several minutes to several hours. Nausea， vomiting， and fever may be present.

【25】Other causes of acute cholecystitis may be typhoid fever 43or a malignant tumor obstructing the biliary tract. Whatever the cause of the obstruction， the normal flow of bile is inter-rupted and the gallbladder becomes distended and ischemic.

【26】Gallstones may also cause chronic cholecystitis (persistent gallbladder inflammation)， in which the gallbladder atro-phies and becomes fibrotic， adhering to adjacent organs. It is not unusual for affected clients to have repeated episodes before seeking medical attention.

【27】**Cholangitis**

【28】Gallstones lodged further down in the system in the common bile duct can cause cholangitis. Blocking the flow of bile at this point in the biliary tree can lead to jaundice. Infection can develop here and travel up to the liver， becoming a poten-tially life-threatening situation.

【65】**Gallbladder Cancer**

【66】Gallbladder cancer， closely associated with gallstone disease， often has a poor outcome because of the delay in diagnosis. The primary associated risk factors include cholelithiasis(especially symptomatic， untreated)， obesity， reproductive abnormalities， chronic gallbladder infection， and exposure to radon and certain industrial exposures including cellulose acetate fiber manufacturing. Testing and treatment of symp-tomatic gallstones is the only preventive measure identified at this time for gallbladder cancer.5

【39】**Developmental regression in toddlers/children**

【40】**· Autism is a major diagnosis of developmental delay or regression in children between the ages of 18 and 26 months； less severely affected individuals may manifest with more limited behavioral deficits at a later age.**

【41】**·Rett syndrome is a major cause of progressive intellectual decline and acquired microcephaly in females， usually starting around 12 months of age.**

【42】**·Developmental regression in childhood is often associated with disorders connected with abnormal accumulation of products of cellular metabolism(lysosomal disorders， neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis) or chronic impairment of energy metabolism (mitochondrial disorders).**

【44】**· Intractable or poorly controlled seizures associated with developmental regression may be a manifestation of a particular etiology or may be idiopathic.**

【45】**·Furthermore， diagnosing untreatable conditions remains important for the purposes of genetic counseling and planning future care.**

【38】**INTRODUCTION**

【39】Tinnitus is a common symptom in primary care， with great heterogeneity in terms of presentation， severity， and etiol-ogy. The term“tinnitus” originates from the Latin word tin-nire， which means“to ring." Although commonly defined as ringing in the ears， a better definition is that“tinnitus is the conscious expression of a sound that originates in an involun-tary manner." 【50】**Symptom-based differential diagnosis may be enhanced by correlating the tinnitus symptoms to origin of the sensation.**

【51】**Conductive System (Outer Ear， Tympanic Membrane， Ossicles)**

【52】Bilateral tinnitus may occur with damage to the conductive hearing system from environmental (prolonged noise expo-sure) or systemic (medications that damage the cochlear hairs) causes. Unilateral tinnitus with conductive hearing loss results from tympanic membrane damage， recurrent unilateral ear infections， ossicle damage， or trauma. Blowing tinnitus may be caused by a patulous (persistently open) eustachian tube， as the tympanic membrane moves in time with the respiratory cycle. Pulsatile or clicking tinnitus may be caused by stape-dius muscle spasm， sometimes up to 175 to 200 contractions per minute.

【53】**Sensorineural Transduction (Cochlea)**

【54】Many cochlear disorders are associated with tinnitus， including Meniere’s disease and postinfectious cochlear labyrinthitis. In addition， many common medications can damage cochlear stereocilia， often irreversibly. With cochlear disorders， spon-taneous otoacoustic emissions (SOAEs) may be heard with a small microphone placed in the patient’s ear canal.

【55】**Central Auditory Pathways Alteration(Eighth Nerve and Brain)**

【56】The closer the focal pathology is to the external ear， the more likely that tinnitus will be unilateral. For instance， unilateral and progressive neurosensory hearing loss may be caused by a tumor that grows out of the myelin sheath of the eighth cranial nerve (called an acoustic neuroma or schwannoma). Alterna-tively， once the auditory pathways have combined in the audi-tory cortex， myelin or axonal brain lesions can produce bilat-eral tinnitus and other neurologic deficits. After head trauma or CNS infections， tinnitus may be caused by nerve sensitivity after cortical reorganization due to auditory disinhibition of normal background sounds. Finally， low serotonin levels may contribute to tinnitus and to depression.

【57】**Referred Sounds**

【58】Not all tinnitus originates in the ear and CNS. Pulsatile tin-nitus may be caused by vascular structures near the ear and high cardiac output states such as pregnancy. Like stapedius myoclonus， palatal myoclonus may also result in a sensation of “clicking” or pulsation.

【3】# 6 Treatment/6.8 Torn pubovaginalis leading to increased use of pubococcygeus, fecal retention/6.8.1 Patient Presentation

【4】### 6.8.1 Patient Presentation

【5】A 50-year-old woman presents with complaints of fecal retention. She states that she feels a progressive bulging within the vagina simultaneously as the rectum pressure progresses. She states that intimacy is often initially uncomfortable but tolerable, and progresses to comfortable. She continues to states that she often places a digit vaginally to assist in the evacuation of the bowel, and that during the more difficult bowel movements she must manually evacuate the rectum using a gloved hand/finger. She admits to having surgical gloves in her purse “all the time.”

【6】# 6 Treatment/6.8 Torn pubovaginalis leading to increased use of pubococcygeus, fecal retention/6.8.2 Evaluation

【7】### 6.8.2 Evaluation

【8】Her history includes three SVDs with grade III fissures to the anus left. Negative loss of urine other than during coughing episodes while ill.

【9】Lumbar evaluation is negative other than an angle of declination of 65 degrees, and crepitus along bilateral SIJ.

【10】Pelvic examination demonstrates a bulge along the posterior vaginal hiatus that increases with volitional contraction of the pelvic floor musculature. There is minimal lift noted. Moderate labial separation noted at rest, increasing with contraction of PFM. External palpation is unremarkable for pain. Separation of the labia minora demonstrates the presence of the distal bowel distending the vaginal canal, occupying more than half the orifice. Upon palpation, it moves easily out of the way, but immediately returns to its fallen/resting position upon release.

【11】Assessment of the PFM indicates significant tone along the posterior margin of the vaginal hiatus and minimal tone along the lateral aspects of the vaginal wall. Layer-to-layer evaluation of the PFM indicates poor overall capacity to contract the first layer of musculature bilaterally, while the second layer was noted to be symmetrical at 3+/5. The third layer demonstrated 3-/5 on the right, while the left was 1/5. There was an absence of bulk throughout the left side of the PFM originating immediately posterior to the pubis, just lateral to the symphysis, while approximately one finger’s breadth lateral thereto is appropriate bulk, albeit with extraordinary tautness, tenderness, and crepitus. Palpation of the anterior SIJ ligament demonstrated course crepitus bilaterally, and Tinel testing of the sacral and pudendal nerves was unremarkable.

【22】Neurological findings were modest. The weakness noted is likely due to the breach of musculature along the left pubovaginalis and the distension of the distal bowel into the vagina, blocking muscle activity. While this is the working assumption, if her strength doesn’t improve, then further neural evaluation is to be conducted and treated as necessary.

【23】Joint restrictions: Sustained central posterior to anterior (CPA) pressure at S3 were conducted both with and without the use of a pelvic floor contraction to assist in a counternutation of the sacrum.

【24】Scars: The scars along the length and origin of the pubovaginalis were addressed with a transverse friction massage. With activation of the pelvic floor musculature, and after the performance of the aforementioned mobilizations, it was found that the remaining fibers of the pubovaginalis responded and hypertrophied over the first three weeks. Local points of scar, denoted via palpation of crepitus, continued to be addressed via transverse friction massage.

【25】The muscle weakness and asymmetry of the pubovaginalis was addressed with manual resistance with a palpating digit. Initially, a stretch facilitation was required. This progressed along well, and to my wonderful surprise, there was a relative restoration of relative bulk and nearly (95%) symmetrical strength.

【26】# 6 Treatment/6.9 Conclusion

【27】6.9 Conclusion
--------------

【28】The purpose of this textbook is to examine the concepts of differential diagnosis and to apply them to the patient with pelvic pain. To do so, a thorough review of the multitude of structures involved with the initiation, perpetuation, and expansion of pelvic pain is discussed so that the clinician can understand and determine what treatment techniques are to be applied to best address the origin of the patient’s pain. When practiced properly, the clinician can expect to make immediate changes in the patient’s well-being, and with proper progression of education, and exercises, these changes can be permanent.

【29】There are no “cookbook” answers to a patients’ pain. Clinicians must learn to accurately determine the initiating and perpetuating aspects of a patient’s pain presentation to most efficiently manage symptoms and provide the patient the opportunity to heal.

【27】**争KEY FACTS**

【28】**_CLINICAL_**

【29】**◆Renal artery stenosis is a common cause of secondary hypertension and is present in 1% to 4% of hyperten-sive patients. It predominantly occurs in whites.**

【30】**◆Renovascular hypertension is produced by excessive renin release， which itself results from a decrease in renal perfusion.**

【31】**◆FFibromuscular hyperplasia is the etiology in 30% of patients who have renovascular hypertension (being more common in women) and is the predominant cause of renovascular hypertension in adults <40 years. In 70% of cases， renovascular hypertension results from atherosclerotic stenosis.**

【32】**◆The following clinical features increase the likelihood that hypertension is secondary to renal artery stenosis：**

【33】**1\. Onset at age <20 and >50 years of age**

【34】**2\. Abdominal bruit**

【35】**3\. Atherosclerotic disease at other sites**

【36】**4\. Abrupt deterioration of renal function after the administration of angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors**

【37】**争Some patients may be managed clinically if renal func-tion does not deteriorate.**

【38】**◆The use of angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors has improved the success rate of medical therapy. However， patients with bilateral renal artery stenosis develop marked hypotension and deterioration of renal function after administration of these agents.**

【39】**Surgical treatment is generally successful， but percuta-neous transluminal angioplasty is now the preferred approach for fibromuscular hyperplasia and discrete atherosclerotic lesions.**

【40】**_RADIOLOGIC_**

【41】**_◆_ Angiography is the gold standard diagnostic procedure for determining renal artery stenosis but has a number of drawbacks： (1) it is an invasive procedure， and (2) it provides an anatomic definition of the arterial luminal diameter but not the physiologic significance of a steno-sis-i.e.， that hypertension is on a renovascular basis.**

【42】**Renal vein renin determination is also an invasive proce-dure and has not proved to be accurate in the diagnosis.**

【43】**专Urography and conventional radionuclide scintigraphy have an unacceptably high rate of false-negative and false-positive results in the diagnosis of renovascular hypertension. Doppler ultrasonography also has vari-able sensitivity and specificity in diagnosis of renovas-cular hypertension.**

【44】**◆Response of hypertension to renal artery angioplasty cannot be predicted from degree of arterial stenosis alone but must be combined with provocative tests such as scintigraphy following administration of angiotensin-converting enzyme. Some patients with mild stenosis but positive angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor scintigraphy have substantial reduc-tion in hypertensin following angioplasty， whereas patients with severe stenoses but negative scintigraphic studies do not generally respond to revascularization.**

【21】KEY FACTS

【22】Clinical

【23】 Epidermoid cysts are thought to arise from inclusion of epithelial elements within the neural groove during its closure.

【24】 Although epidermoid cysts grow with age, they are not considered neoplasms. Enlargement occurs due to progressive accumulation of breakdown products of desquamated epithelial cells, including keratin and solid cholesterol.

【25】 Eighty percent of intracranial epidermoid cysts are intradural in location, often appearing in the infraten-torial compartment. The cerebellopontine angle is one of the more common sites. 【26】 Epidermoid cysts are slow-growing lesions that conform to the surface of the brain as they enlarge, infiltrate through the subarachnoid space, and surround vessels and cranial nerves. Symptoms have often been present for many months or a few years by the time of discovery.

【27】 Because the surfaces of intracranial epidermoid cysts have a shiny, white surface appearance, they are sometimes referred to as “pearly tumors.”

【28】 Epidermoid cysts are similar to dermoid cysts in that both lesions have a stratified squamous epithelial lining with a fibrous connective tissue capsule, but epidermoid cysts lack sebaceous and sweat gland secretory units.

【29】 Arachnoid cyst is the principal diagnostic consideration from which epidermoid cyst must be distinguished. Arachnoid cysts are frequently not treated due to the fact that they are asymptomatic, stable congenital lesions. Epidermoid cysts, however, are often symptomatic and continue to grow with advancing age, necessitating resection.

【30】 Total surgical resection of an epidermoid cyst is often impossible because portions of the lesion are buried in spaces that cannot be reached without causing undue traction on important neurologic or vascular structures. Furthermore, and because the tumor is often tightly adherent to brain and blood vessels. In those instances, partial debulking is performed, which may need to be repeated as the lesion regrows.

【31】Radiologic

【32】 On unenhanced head CT, epidermoid cysts are hypodense extra-axial masses whose margins are often slightly lobulated or scalloped. Many lesions are slightly hyperdense relative to CSF and mildly inhomogeneous. However, they frequently are isodense to CSF, making distinction from arachnoid cyst difficult. Occasionally, a very small amount of calcification can be seen.

【33】 Epidermoid cysts have a soft, pliable consistency, but they often exert a moderate degree of mass effect on adjacent brain structures. Multilocular lesions are seen in about 20% of cases.

【34】 Lack of enhancement after contrast administration is the general rule; very mild contrast-enhancement can be seen around the rim of the lesion in about 30% of cases.

【35】 MRI is frequently useful in distinguishing epidermoid cysts from arachnoid cysts because the lesion often appears inhomogeneous and has a signal intensity that differs from CSF on at least one pulse. The most common pulse sequences on which the signal intensity of the lesion differs from that of CSF are FLAIR, proton density-weighted and diffusion-weighted sequences.

【36】 MRI is important in surgical planning because it is the best method for defining the limits of the mass and the spatial relationship to cranial nerves and blood vessels.

【37】 Lesions involving the cerebellopontine angle often extend into Meckel’s cave.

【38】 When a suspected epidermoid cyst is isointense with CSF on all pulse sequences, the distinction from arachnoid cyst can be made by pulse sequences that are sensitive to water motion—for example, diffusion-weighted images and steady-state free precession images. On diffusion-weighted images, the apparent diffusion coefficient values of epidermoid cysts are typically much lower than those of CSF but often only mildly elevated or even mildly decreased compared to brain tissue.
